title: The Shallow End of August
author: Mara Quist
hook: Every morning she swims the same eight lengths. This August, someone is waiting at the deep end.
blurb:
Since her divorce, Nora Bell has lived by the pool's black lines: eight lengths at six, coffee at seven, no surprises. Then her estranged son moves back to town and starts swimming in the lane beside hers.
Over one hot, unhurried month, mother and son circle the things they never said, length by length, until the water has nowhere left to hide them.
bio: Mara Quist grew up in a seaside town in Western Australia and taught swimming for nine summers before she wrote a word. This is her first novel.

title: The Absent Sitter
author: Celia Vanderhoek
hook: The portrait is famous. The woman in it vanished the year it was painted.
blurb:
In 1898 Isabel Hart sat for a fashionable society portrait. A month later she was gone, and her family cut her out of every letter, ledger and photograph.
A century on, a conservator cleaning the painting finds something beneath the varnish that does not belong there. To learn who Isabel really was, she must first ask why so many people needed her to disappear.
bio: Celia Vanderhoek trained as a paintings conservator in Amsterdam and New York. She now writes full time from a studio above a frame shop. This is her first novel.

title: Low Sky
author: Wren Adair
hook: On the plains, weather is the only thing that ever arrives.
blurb:
After her mother's stroke, Ada drives back to the farm she swore she'd never see again: forty miles of wheat, one road, and a sky so low it seems to sit on the roof.
As a storm season builds and the family debts come due, Ada learns the land keeps its own records, and the people who stayed have been reading them all along.
bio: Wren Adair was raised on a farm in northern Oklahoma. She has worked as a storm spotter, a court reporter and a bookseller. Low Sky is her first novel.

title: Say the Quiet Part
author: Odile Brennan
hook: Somebody in this family has to say it. It might as well be the one who never talks.
blurb:
The Brennans are loud: loud at weddings, loud at funerals, loudest of all about nothing. Only Tess, the youngest, has spent thirty years listening.
When her father's seventieth birthday brings everyone home for one long weekend, Tess finally decides to speak, and the family discovers that the quietest voice in the room has kept the loudest secrets.
Funny, sharp and full of heart, it is a novel for anyone who has ever been the quiet one at a loud table.
bio: Odile Brennan is the youngest of six. She lives in Galway, where she teaches drama and is told, often, that she is too quiet. This is her first novel.

title: Blue Hour at the Hotel Ostend
author: Pia Lindqvist
hook: Between the last light and the first lamp, two strangers have one hour.
blurb:
Every evening at the Hotel Ostend, a widowed translator watches the light go blue through the shutters. Every evening, the man in Room 14 does the same.
They never speak in daylight. But over one winter on the Belgian coast, their blue-hour conversations become the truest thing in either life, until the season ends and the hotel prepares to close for good.
bio: Pia Lindqvist was born in Gothenburg and has lived on four coastlines. She translates poetry from Swedish and French. Blue Hour at the Hotel Ostend is her first novel in English.

title: Gently, Gently
author: Tomasz Ilić
hook: Some things can only be held if you don't hold them too tightly.
blurb:
Marek has been a careful man all his life: careful with money, with words, with his daughter Ana. When Ana comes home pregnant and unwilling to say who the father is, careful is no longer enough.
Set over one autumn in a small Croatian town, this is a tender, prickly novel about the ways we protect the people we love, and the ways we hurt them doing it.
bio: Tomasz Ilić was born in Zagreb and grew up in Kraków. He works as a hospital interpreter and writes in the early mornings. Gently, Gently is his first novel.

title: Field Notes on Leaving
author: Agnes Thorvald
hook: She catalogued every fern in the valley. She never wrote down why she left.
blurb:
In 1852 a young woman makes blueprints of ferns, pressing them into paper with nothing but sunlight. In 2024 her great-great-granddaughter finds the notebook, and a list of places she was never meant to go.
Moving between two women and two centuries, Field Notes on Leaving is a novel about what we record, what we keep, and the courage it takes to walk away.
bio: Agnes Thorvald is a botanist turned writer. She grew up in Norway, lives in Scotland and owns more pressed flowers than furniture. Field Notes on Leaving is her first novel.

title: The Other Half of Ines
author: Lucía Ferrand
hook: At eighty-six, Ines decides to tell the other half of the story.
blurb:
Everyone in the village knows Ines Ferrand: widow, baker, keeper of the church keys. No one knows about the summer of 1958, or the woman she almost left with.
When a young journalist arrives to record the village's oldest voices, Ines finally has someone to tell. But the truth has a way of changing the past for everyone who is still living in it.
bio: Lucía Ferrand grew up in Valencia and spent ten years recording oral histories in rural Spain. She now lives in Lisbon. This is her first novel.

title: A Room Without Weather
author: Hal Okonjo
hook: The first thing he noticed was the cloud in the spare room.
blurb:
Three weeks after his wife's death, Joseph opens the door to the room she used for painting and finds a small grey cloud hovering above the floorboards. It rains a little on Tuesdays.
His children think he is losing his mind. Joseph thinks he might finally be finding it. A strange, warm and quietly funny novel about grief, and what it leaves in the house.
bio: Hal Okonjo was born in Lagos and lives in Leeds. He has been a meteorologist, a radio presenter and a reluctant gardener. He is working on a second novel.

title: All the Borrowed Cups
author: June Mbeki
hook: Every cup in Grace's kitchen belongs to someone else. So does her life.
blurb:
Grace has never owned a cup. She has borrowed them from neighbours, lovers, landladies and a hospital canteen, and returned none of them.
When the cupboard finally overflows, she sets out to give every cup back, one owner at a time. A bright, funny and unexpectedly moving novel about what we take from each other, and what we're brave enough to return.
bio: June Mbeki was born in Durban and lives in Cape Town, where she runs a small café with very mismatched crockery. This is her debut novel.

title: The Saint of Small Repairs
author: Benedek Oravecz
hook: He fixed every broken thing in the village. He never fixed himself.
blurb:
For forty years Benedek has mended the town's clocks, chairs, radios and hearts in a workshop that smells of oil and pipe smoke. Nobody ever asks what he lost in 1956.
When a boy brings in a music box that once belonged to Benedek's sister, the old man must open the one thing he swore never to repair.
A gentle, luminous novel about the things we cannot mend, and the ones we finally can.
bio: Benedek Oravecz grew up in Pécs and trained as a watchmaker before he wrote fiction. He lives in Budapest with a cat named Rivet. This is his second novel.

title: The Lemon Grove Supper Club
author: Rosa Delacroix-Hale
hook: Eight seats. Seven strangers. One secret on the menu.
blurb:
Every Thursday, in a lemon grove above the Amalfi coast, Rosa Ferrante serves dinner to eight guests who have never met. The rule is simple: everyone brings a story, and nobody leaves until it's told.
Then an Englishwoman books a seat with a story that is about Rosa herself. A sunny, generous novel about food, family and the courage to set one more place.
bio: Rosa Delacroix-Hale has cooked in kitchens in Naples, Lyon and London. She lives in Kent with her husband and an ambitious lemon tree. This is her first novel.

title: Mrs. Penhallow Says No
author: Gwen Abernathy
hook: Seventy-nine years of saying yes. Starting today, she's done.
blurb:
Edith Penhallow has said yes to every committee, every grandchild, every neighbour with a casserole dish to fill. Then, on her seventy-ninth birthday, she says no.
No to the church bake sale. No to selling the house. No to the son who thinks she should be in a home. One small word sets off a big, funny, life-changing summer for everyone in Little Bassett.
bio: Gwen Abernathy is a former school secretary who has said yes far too often. She lives in Cornwall and is practising. This is her first novel, written mostly in the garden.

title: Sunny Side, Mostly
author: Della Okafor
hook: Breakfast for dinner. Mum's rule for the bad days. These days, they're all bad.
blurb:
When their mother walks out, sixteen-year-old Joy and her little brother keep the house running on fried eggs, lists and lies. Nobody at school needs to know. Nobody at all.
Told over one year of breakfasts, Sunny Side, Mostly is a warm and funny novel about two kids holding a family together, and the neighbour who notices.
Some days are harder than others. Most days, there are eggs.
bio: Della Okafor grew up in Manchester as the eldest of four. She is a social worker and writes on her lunch breaks. She still makes breakfast for dinner.

title: Postcards from Aunt Vera
author: Nadia Ferro
hook: Aunt Vera sent a postcard from every city she ever ran away to.
blurb:
When eccentric Aunt Vera dies, she leaves her niece Clara a shoebox of postcards, a plane ticket to Venice and one instruction: follow them in order.
From a canal-side apartment to a pink-skied coast in France, Clara retraces the life of the woman her family never talked about, and finds out exactly why Vera kept moving.
Funny, sun-drenched and full of surprises, it is a love letter to the aunts who never stayed put.
bio: Nadia Ferro was born in Turin and raised in Toronto. She has lived in eleven cities and kept a postcard from each. This is her debut novel.

title: Every Light in the House
author: Imogen Castell
hook: The Castell house has twelve windows. For twenty years, only one has been lit.
blurb:
After their father's funeral, three estranged sisters return to the house on Hollin Lane to clear it out in a single weekend. None of them expects the lamp in the attic to be on.
Over three nights, as they open boxes, old rooms and old wounds, the sisters discover why their mother kept that one light burning.
A moving novel about sisters, secrets and the lights we leave on for each other.
bio: Imogen Castell is the middle of three sisters. She grew up in the Yorkshire Dales and now lives in Bristol. She always leaves a light on.

title: Ask Me Again on Tuesday
author: Maya Lindgren
hook: Every Tuesday he asks. Every Tuesday she says, ask me again.
blurb:
Eva runs a flower stall at the market. Tom sells cheese at the stall beside it. Every Tuesday for a year, he has asked her to dinner. Every Tuesday, she has told him to ask her again.
But Eva isn't playing hard to get. She is counting down to a day only she knows about. A tender, funny love story with a clock ticking under it.
bio: Maya Lindgren grew up above her parents' bakery in Malmö. She now lives in London and keeps a calendar she never looks at. This is her first novel.

title: Lost & Found at Platform 4
author: Ruth Ellery-Shaw
hook: Everything left on a train ends up in Ruth's office. Including, one day, a man.
blurb:
For thirty years Ruth has run the lost property office at a small northern station: umbrellas, teeth, a stuffed heron. Nothing surprises her.
Then a gentle stranger arrives who cannot remember his name, only that he was meant to meet someone on Platform 4. Ruth decides to find out who, and finds a great deal more than she bargained for.
bio: Ruth Ellery-Shaw worked for the railways for twenty-two years. She lives in Carlisle with a husband and two spare umbrellas. This is her first novel, written on the 7:52 train.

title: A House Full of Summers
author: Clementine Ashby
hook: One house. Four generations. Every summer they swore would be the last.
blurb:
Every August, the Ashby family returns to the old house by the woods: the grandparents, the bickering siblings, the cousins who only meet once a year.
This summer, Grandma Clem announces the house is to be sold, and everyone has one month to decide what it was worth to them. A big-hearted family novel full of picnics, quarrels and the long light of August.
bio: Clementine Ashby has spent every summer of her life in the same family house in Somerset. She writes there now. This is her first novel, finished on the porch.

title: Don't Tell Mum Yet
author: Ottilie Grange
hook: The phone rang at 2 a.m. Three sisters agreed: Mum must never find out.
blurb:
Their mother has a weak heart and a strong opinion about everything. So when the youngest sister lands in hot water, the other two decide to sort it out before Mum hears a word.
There's just one problem: Mum always hears. A fast, funny novel about sisters, secrets and the lengths we go to protect the people who'd rather we just told the truth.
bio: Ottilie Grange is one of three sisters and has kept many things from her mother. She lives in Brighton. Her mother has not read this book.

title: Seven at the Table
author: Harriet Mwangi
hook: They always set seven places. This Christmas, someone has to sit in the empty chair.
blurb:
For twelve years the Mwangi family has laid a place for Daniel, the brother who left one Christmas Eve and never came back.
This year a letter arrives: he is coming home for dinner. Over one tense, funny, heartbreaking evening, a family must decide whether they want the brother they lost, or the story they have told about him.
Pass the potatoes. Mind the chair.
bio: Harriet Mwangi grew up in Nairobi and London in a family that never stopped talking at dinner. She lives in Leicester. This is her first novel.

title: The Matchmaker of Rue Delphine
author: Céline Marchand
hook: She has made two hundred matches on Rue Delphine. Her own isn't one of them.
blurb:
Madame Colette has run a discreet matchmaking business above a Paris flower shop for forty years, and she has never once been wrong.
Then her newest client turns out to be the man she sent away in 1979. A charming, romantic novel about second chances, red geraniums and the one match nobody saw coming.
Some matches take two hundred tries. Some take forty-five years and one very stubborn heart.
bio: Céline Marchand was born in Lyon and has lived in Paris for twenty years, always above a shop of some kind. She has introduced three couples who are still married.

title: The Glass Daughter of Murano
author: Livia Contarini
hook: On an island of glassmakers, the greatest secret is a girl who can blow fire.
blurb:
Murano, 1510. Glassmakers are forbidden to leave the island, and daughters are forbidden to touch the furnace. Lucia Contarini breaks both rules every night.
When a commission from the Doge threatens to ruin her family, Lucia must make the impossible: a bowl as blue as the lagoon, painted with dancing figures, and finished before anyone learns whose breath shaped it.
bio: Livia Contarini grew up in Venice and studied art history in Padua. Her grandfather worked a furnace on Murano for fifty years. This is her first novel.

title: The Cartographer of Lost Rivers
author: Teodora Vasari
hook: Rome, 1748. A mapmaker is paid to draw every street. And to leave one river out.
blurb:
Young Matteo is the best draughtsman in Nolli's workshop, measuring every alley of Rome for the great new map. Then a cardinal pays him a fortune to erase a buried stream from the plan.
Following the lost river through cellars, churches and secret wells, Matteo uncovers what the water was hiding, and why someone would kill to keep it off the map.
bio: Teodora Vasari was born in Florence and trained as an architect. She has walked every street on Nolli's 1748 map of Rome. This is her first novel.

title: The Rivet Girls
author: Dorothy Kowalczyk
hook: Detroit, 1943. They built bombers by day. By night, they built something bigger.
blurb:
When the men ship out, four women walk into a Detroit aircraft plant and pick up rivet guns for the first time. They learn to hold a line of metal, a shift, and each other.
But when one of them is hurt and the company covers it up, the Rivet Girls decide to fight a battle no one expected them to win.
A stirring novel of friendship and courage on the home front.
bio: Dorothy Kowalczyk grew up in Hamtramck, Michigan. Her grandmother riveted bomber wings at the Willow Run plant in 1943. This is her first novel. She lives in Ann Arbor.

title: The Silk Merchant's Wife
author: Hana Moriyama
hook: Edo, 1798. She married for silk. She stayed for something far more dangerous.
blurb:
Sayo is famous in the pleasure quarter for her beauty and her poems. When a rich silk merchant buys her contract, she exchanges one gilded cage for another.
But the merchant's house hides debts, rivals and a ledger that could ruin half of Edo. Sayo learns that a woman who can read accounts is far more dangerous than one who can write verses.
bio: Hana Moriyama grew up in Kyoto and Vancouver. She researches Edo-period merchant records and writes historical fiction. She lives in Vancouver with her family and a shelf of old account books.

title: Portrait of Lady Sorrel
author: Eleanor Fairfax-Lowe
hook: The painting shows a perfect wife. The woman in it had other plans.
blurb:
Bath, 1774. Lady Anne Sorrel is to be painted by the most fashionable artist in England, a portrait meant to show the world her husband's wealth and her obedience.
Over twelve sittings, painter and sitter begin a battle of wills on canvas. What Anne wants the picture to say could change both their lives, if anyone learns to read it.
bio: Eleanor Fairfax-Lowe studied Georgian portraiture at the Courtauld and once spent a year cleaning gilt frames. She lives in Bath. This is her first novel, set in the city she loves.

title: The Wolves of Aldgate
author: Thomas Ashgrove
hook: London, 1536. The wolves at the city gate are not the ones with teeth.
blurb:
When a merchant is found dead beneath the bronze wolf's head on Aldgate, the coroner calls it an accident. His apprentice, Kit, knows better.
As Henry VIII's men tear down the monasteries and fortunes change hands overnight, Kit follows a trail of forged deeds into the most dangerous houses in Tudor London.
In a city where loyalty changes with the king's mood, trust nobody who smiles.
bio: Thomas Ashgrove is a former archivist at a London livery company. He lives near the line of the old city wall. This is his first novel.

title: Ration Book Summer
author: Peggy Hollis-Ward
hook: Summer, 1944. One ration book, two families, and a lie that feeds them both.
blurb:
In bomb-scarred Wapping, Peggy Hollis-Ward feeds four children on one book of coupons and a lot of nerve. When a stranger's ration book falls into her hands, she makes a choice that keeps her family alive.
But the book belongs to someone, and that someone is coming to collect. A warm and gripping novel of the home front.
Moving, funny and full of the grit of wartime London, it is a story of mothers who did whatever it took.
bio: Peggy Hollis-Ward grew up on stories of the Blitz from her grandmother, a Wapping greengrocer. She lives in Essex. She collects wartime cookbooks. This is her first novel.

title: What the Potter Broke
author: Ione Papadakis
hook: Athens, 520 BC. One shard survived. This is the story it remembers.
blurb:
In the potters' quarter of Athens, a slave girl named Ione grinds the black slip for a famous painter. She is not allowed to hold a brush.
When the master's hand begins to fail, Ione secretly paints his last great vase, a god with a lyre, and sets in motion a scandal that will shatter far more than clay.
Based on a real fragment of painted clay, this is a story of art, ambition and the hands history forgets.
bio: Ione Papadakis is an archaeologist who has spent twelve summers digging in Attica. She lives in Athens and Edinburgh. This is her first novel. She is writing her second.

title: A Sampler of Small Mercies
author: Elspeth Rowe
hook: Every stitch was a word she was not allowed to say.
blurb:
Yorkshire, 1846. Twelve-year-old Elspeth is sent to a charity school where girls are taught silence, scripture and needlework.
Through the sampler she stitches over one hard year, a house, two trees and a row of letters, Elspeth hides a record of everything she sees. A century and a half later, someone finally learns how to read it.
A quiet, devastating novel about girlhood, courage and the stories hidden in plain sight.
bio: Elspeth Rowe is a textile historian who has catalogued over four hundred Victorian samplers. She lives in the Yorkshire Dales. She stitches every evening. This is her first novel.

title: The Cipher Girls
author: Margaret Ellison-Byrne
hook: Bletchley, 1941. They broke the code. Then they broke the rules.
blurb:
Three young women arrive at a country house in Buckinghamshire to do work they can never describe. Peg can solve any crossword; Ada speaks four languages; Joan just wants to be useful.
When they intercept a message about one of their own, the Cipher Girls must decide how much they will risk to save her, and how much they can keep secret forever.
bio: Margaret Ellison-Byrne's aunt worked at Bletchley Park and never said a word until she was eighty. Margaret lives in Oxford. The Cipher Girls is her first novel.

title: The Last Gilded Party
author: Vivienne Laroque
hook: Paris, October 1929. The champagne is still flowing. The money already isn't.
blurb:
Vivienne Laroque throws the best parties in Paris: jazz, gold dresses and guests who never ask who is paying. This one will be her last, and only she knows it.
As the stock market wobbles across the ocean, Vivienne has one night to settle a fortune, a marriage and a lie she has kept for ten glittering years.
Glittering, heartbreaking and full of jazz, it is the last night of an age.
bio: Vivienne Laroque was born in Montréal and studied in Paris, where she now lives in a flat with a very small balcony. This is her first novel.

title: Still Water, Late Light
author: Margit Solberg
hook: Every evening the pond gives back the sky. This summer it gives back something else.
blurb:
After forty years of marriage, Astrid comes alone to the lake house in the Norwegian hills where she and her husband spent every July. She swims at dawn, paints at dusk and talks to no one.
Then her grown daughter arrives without warning, carrying a letter that changes the meaning of every summer they ever spent there. A luminous, slow-burning novel about long marriages, late truths and the light that comes after.
bio: Margit Solberg grew up in Bergen and studied painting in Oslo. She now divides her year between a city flat and a lake house with no phone signal. This is her first novel.

title: A Short History of Leaving
author: Nell Okafor-Vance
hook: She has left eleven homes, four countries and one husband. She has never once said goodbye.
blurb:
Ada Vance is very good at leaving. She can pack a life into two suitcases in an afternoon and be gone before anyone notices. It is staying she has never learned.
When her father falls ill in the town she fled at eighteen, Ada finally has to stop. Told in eleven departures and one long return, this is a sharp, funny and tender novel about the art of letting go.
bio: Nell Okafor-Vance was born in Lagos, grew up in Leeds and has lived in nine cities since. She works as a translator and has finally bought furniture. This is her first novel.

title: The Widows' Tea Society
author: Hattie Greenwood
hook: Three widows. One teapot. And a husband who isn't quite as dead as they thought.
blurb:
Every Thursday at four, Edna, Marjorie and Pearl meet for tea and complaints in Edna's front room. They have buried three husbands between them and have no intention of finding a fourth.
Then Pearl's late husband is spotted alive and well at the seaside. What follows is a gloriously funny, warm-hearted caper about friendship, second chances and the strength of a very good pot of tea.
bio: Hattie Greenwood is a retired district nurse who has drunk tea in a thousand front rooms across Shropshire. She lives with her sister and a very old dog. This is her first novel.

title: Nonna's Recipe for Starting Over
author: Gianna Russo-Bell
hook: Two cups of courage. One old suitcase. And a family recipe nobody has ever got right.
blurb:
When her marriage ends and her bakery fails in the same week, Lucia goes home to Puglia with one suitcase and nowhere else to go. Her grandmother hands her a stained recipe card and a single instruction: start again.
One summer, one kitchen and one very bossy nonna later, Lucia learns that some recipes are not about food at all. A warm, delicious novel to read with a slice of something good.
bio: Gianna Russo-Bell grew up between Bari and Boston in a family of very loud cooks. She ran a small bakery for ten years before she started writing. This is her first novel.

title: The Tulip Merchant's Debt
author: Saskia van Loon
hook: Haarlem, 1637. One tulip bulb is worth a house. By Friday, it will be worth nothing.
blurb:
In the winter of 1637, all of Holland has gone mad for tulips. Young Pieter de Vries has signed a promissory note for a single bulb worth more than his father's house.
When the market crashes overnight, Pieter must find the bulb, the buyer and the truth behind the most beautiful flower in the Netherlands before his debt destroys everyone he loves. A vivid, gripping novel of greed and beauty in the Dutch Golden Age.
bio: Saskia van Loon is a Dutch economic historian who has spent years in the archives of Haarlem. She lives in Leiden with her family and an unreasonable number of bulbs. This is her first novel.

title: The Last Joust at Ashby
author: Hugh Ravensworth
hook: England, 1524. One last tournament. One knight who must not win.
blurb:
Sir Edmund Ashby was the greatest jouster of the old king's court. Now he is old, in debt, and summoned to ride one final tournament before King Henry.
His son is meant to win in his place. But the joust has been rigged, and Edmund learns that the lance aimed at his family will not be the one in the lists. A thrilling Tudor novel of honour, armour and betrayal.
bio: Hugh Ravensworth spent twenty years as an armour conservator at a national museum. He has handled helmets older than most castles. He lives in Yorkshire. This is his first novel.

title: Plus One, No Strings
author: Poppy Carrington
hook: She needs a date for the wedding. He needs a fake fiancée. What could go wrong?
blurb:
Poppy has three weeks to find a plus one for her sister's wedding, or face her ex and his new wife alone. Enter Sam, her infuriating neighbour, who needs someone to pretend to be engaged to him for exactly the same weekend.
The rules are simple: one weekend, no feelings, no strings. They last about four hours.
A fake engagement, a real disaster, and the most romantic wedding weekend of the year.
bio: Poppy Carrington writes funny, warm love stories from a flat in Manchester. She has been a bridesmaid eleven times. She has never once had a plus one.

title: Out of Office, Into Trouble
author: Jess Okoro
hook: Her auto-reply says she's in Greece. Her boss is in the next sun lounger.
blurb:
Workaholic Jess books her first holiday in six years: two weeks on a Greek island with no laptop, no email, and definitely no Leo Hart, the boss who drives her up the wall.
The universe has other plans. Sun, sea, one very small villa and a lot of very large feelings. Out of office has never felt so dangerous.
Pack your sun cream. You'll need it.
bio: Jess Okoro works in marketing in London and has never once switched her out-of-office on properly. This is her debut. She is currently on holiday.

title: Meet Me at the Laundromat
author: Sunny Abara
hook: Lost: one sock. Found: the love of her life.
blurb:
Every Sunday night, Ada does her laundry at the 24-hour laundromat on Ferry Road. Every Sunday night, so does the grumpy man with the cello case.
When their socks get mixed up in machine four, a string of notes left in the lost-and-found box turns into the sweetest, silliest courtship in the city. A cosy, heart-warming rom-com.
Sweet, funny and as warm as clothes fresh from the dryer.
bio: Sunny Abara lives in Leeds, where she teaches primary school and loses at least one sock a week. This is her first novel. She is writing her second.

title: Thorn & Vow
author: Sloane Mercer
hook: He swore to destroy her family. Then he swore to marry her.
blurb:
Wren Hale was raised to hate the Mercer family, and Cassian Mercer most of all. When her father's debts fall into his hands, Cassian offers her one way out: marry him.
Their vows are a contract. Their marriage is a war. But every thorn has a rose behind it, and Cassian's secrets are sharper than either of them expected.
An enemies-to-lovers dark romance with a marriage of convenience at its heart.
bio: Sloane Mercer writes dark, slow-burn romance with very sharp edges. She lives in the north of England with two black cats. Thorn & Vow is her debut.

title: The Ruthless Move
author: Vera Kostova
tagline: Book one of the Black Court
hook: In his world, every move is a sacrifice. She won't be his pawn.
blurb:
Nika Volkova is a chess prodigy who plays for money in the back rooms of the city. Lev Orlov owns those rooms, and he never loses.
When Nika beats him in front of his men, Lev offers her a deal she can't refuse. One game a week. One secret for every win. Book one of the Black Court.
A dark, slow-burn romance where every game is played for keeps.
bio: Vera Kostova grew up in Sofia playing chess with her grandfather. She writes dark romance late at night. This is the first book in the Black Court series.

title: A Crown of Moth & Ember
author: Isolde Vane
hook: The moth queen was born to burn. The ember prince was born to put her out.
blurb:
In the court of Ember, flame-wielders rule and the moth-folk serve. Isra is the last of a line that can turn fire into light, and the crown wants her in chains.
When the cold-hearted heir is ordered to bring her in, neither of them expects the bargain they strike, or the fire it lights. The first book in the Ember Court series.
bio: Isolde Vane writes romantic fantasy full of courts, curses and slow-burning love. She lives in Wales, close to a very old forest. This is the first book in the Ember Court series.

title: The Thorned Heir
author: Rowan Ashdown
hook: To claim the throne, she must kill him. To survive, she must love him.
blurb:
Every heir of the Thorn Kingdom must win the crown with one blade. Rowan has trained for this all her life: one duel, one death, one throne.
But her rival is the exiled prince who saved her life as a child, and the dagger she carries is cursed to choose its own victim. A sweeping romantasy of blood, roses and fate.
bio: Rowan Ashdown writes epic romantic fantasy. She has fenced since she was eleven and still holds a blade better than a pen. This is her first romantasy.

title: A Rake's Guide to Ruin
author: Arabella Quill
hook: Rule one: never fall for the rake. Rule two: see rule one.
blurb:
London, 1814. Lady Clara Wynn has written an anonymous guide to the most dangerous rakes in society, and the ton is reading every word.
The most dangerous of them all, the Earl of Ashcombe, has vowed to unmask the author. Clara has vowed to ruin him first. Neither of them has read the final chapter.
Sparkling, witty and full of Regency mischief, it is the season's most scandalous read.
bio: Arabella Quill writes witty Regency romance. She lives in Bath, owns three fans and has never been ruined. This is her first novel. She is writing her second.

title: Profile of a Scandal
author: Lady Henrietta Doyle
hook: One cameo. Two faces. A scandal all of London is wearing.
blurb:
When a jeweller carves a cameo of two lovers, it becomes the most fashionable brooch in London, and the most dangerous. Everyone knows the profiles: the widowed Lady Henrietta and the notorious Captain Doyle.
The trouble is, they have never met. Now they must pretend to be in love to stop the gossip, or be ruined trying.
Fake courtship, real feelings and the finest gossip in Regency London.
bio: Lady Henrietta Doyle is the pen name of a Wedgwood collector who writes historical romance from a cottage in Staffordshire. She has never been involved in a scandal. Probably.

title: Same Pier, Next Summer
author: Marisol Vega
hook: Ten years ago they said goodbye on this pier. They promised: same time next summer.
blurb:
Maya and Ben spent every childhood summer at the lake, until the August that ended everything. Now Maya is back to sell her grandmother's cottage, and Ben is the only builder in town.
One summer, one pier, and one promise neither of them has forgotten. A warm, aching second-chance love story.
Some promises are made to be broken. Some are made to be kept, ten years late.
bio: Marisol Vega spent every summer of her childhood at a lake in Michigan. She now lives in Chicago and writes love stories. This is her first novel.

title: Two Minutes for Kissing
author: Kenzie Laird
hook: Two minutes in the penalty box. A lifetime to make it up to her.
blurb:
Kenzie Laird is the new physio for the city's hockey team, and she has one rule: never date a player. Captain Rhys MacLeod has spent his career breaking rules.
When a hit on the ice sends Rhys to her treatment table for six weeks, the rink gets very warm. A funny, steamy sports romance.
He has always played rough. She has always played it safe. This season, both of them are about to lose.
bio: Kenzie Laird is a former team physiotherapist from Edinburgh. She has watched a lot of hockey and taped up a lot of hockey players. This is her debut.

title: An Affair at Fontainebleau
author: Delphine Aubrac
hook: A royal hunt. A forbidden kiss. A secret the whole court is watching.
blurb:
Fontainebleau, 1725. Painter's daughter Louise is hired to sketch the king's autumn hunt. The Comte de Valmy is hired to keep an eye on her.
Among the falling leaves and gilded picnics, a forbidden love blooms in the one place where nothing is ever private. A lush, romantic historical romance.
Every sketch she makes of him is a confession. Every glance he gives her could cost him everything.
bio: Delphine Aubrac studied eighteenth-century French painting in Paris and writes romance set in its golden age. She lives in Paris with her husband and a very spoiled dog.

title: Still Behind Us
author: Nadia Forsythe
tagline: Objects in mirror are closer than they appear
hook: Don't look back. Whatever you do, don't stop.
blurb:
Driving home on a dark country road, Hannah sees headlights in her mirror. They follow her for forty miles, then vanish at her gate.
The next night they are back. The police say she is imagining it. Her husband says she is tired. Only Hannah knows the car belongs to a man who died ten years ago.
A relentless, nerve-shredding thriller that will make you check your mirrors twice.
bio: Nadia Forsythe writes psychological thrillers. She lives on a very long, very dark road in rural Scotland. She checks her mirrors constantly. This is her first novel.

title: Lights On at Number Nine
author: Callum Rhys
hook: Every light in the building is off. Except one.
blurb:
Insomniac Callum watches the tower block opposite every night. At 3 a.m., every window is dark except number nine, where a red lamp burns until dawn.
One night the lamp goes out. The next morning, the flat is empty, the tenant has never existed, and someone has started watching Callum back.
Gripping, claustrophobic and twisty to the very last page.
bio: Callum Rhys lives on the eleventh floor of a block in Cardiff and sleeps very badly. This is his first thriller. He is writing his second.

title: What She Left Out
author: Ruth Abernethy-Cole
hook: Her statement was four pages long. The truth was in the gaps.
blurb:
When a teenager disappears from a wedding party, every guest gives a statement. Ruth's is perfect: clear, calm, consistent.
Detective Anna Cole reads it twelve times before she notices what's missing. A cool, clever psychological thriller about the stories women tell to survive, and the lines they black out.
Read every line. Then read the ones that aren't there.
Nothing is redacted by accident.
bio: Ruth Abernethy-Cole spent fifteen years as a court stenographer. She knows exactly how much people leave out. This is her first novel. She lives in Glasgow.

title: The 11:40 Ferry
author: Ingrid Halvorsen
hook: Twelve passengers boarded the last ferry. Eleven got off.
blurb:
Every night the 11:40 ferry crosses the fjord in fog. Tonight it arrives one passenger short, and no one admits to seeing anyone go over the side.
Detective Ingrid Moen has until the morning sailing to question eleven strangers who all have something to hide. A twisting locked-room mystery on open water.
The fog is thick. The water is cold. And one of the eleven is lying.
bio: Ingrid Halvorsen grew up on an island near Bergen and took the ferry to school every day. She writes crime fiction. This is her first novel in English.

title: The Breath on the Glass
author: Eliza Moreau
hook: Someone wrote her name on the window. From the outside.
blurb:
Eliza lives alone on the nineteenth floor. One winter morning she finds words written in the fog on her bedroom window, words only her dead sister ever knew.
As the messages keep coming, Eliza must decide whether she is being haunted, hunted or slowly driven mad. A chilling, claustrophobic thriller.
Keep your windows closed. Keep your breath to yourself.
Some messages are meant for one reader only.
bio: Eliza Moreau writes psychological suspense. She lives in a high-rise in Lyon and keeps her curtains closed. This is her first novel in English. She lives alone.

title: Have You Seen June?
author: Tess Dumarais
hook: Her poster is on every pole in town. Someone keeps tearing her face off.
blurb:
Seventeen-year-old June Ashby vanished walking home from a party. Her sister Tess puts up two hundred posters. By morning, the photo has been ripped from every one.
The police say it's kids. Tess knows it's a message. And the town that loved June is hiding exactly what happened on Harlow Road.
A gripping small-town thriller about sisters, secrets and the faces we choose not to see.
bio: Tess Dumarais grew up in a small town in Maine where everyone knew everyone. She writes thrillers about small towns. This is her first novel, written over three long winters.

title: The Other Cabin
author: Annika Lund
hook: From the dock you can see one cabin. In the water, there are two.
blurb:
Annika rents a lakeside cabin to finish her book in peace. Every evening she sees a light in the reflection of the cabin across the lake.
The trouble is, there's no cabin across the lake. A slow-burning, eerie thriller about grief, solitude and what the water remembers.
Haunting, atmospheric and impossible to put down.
Some reflections show what is really there. Some show what is coming.
bio: Annika Lund grew up in Swedish lake country and spends her summers in a cabin with no electricity. She writes suspense. This is her first novel in English.

title: The Seating Plan
author: Philippa Strand
hook: Twelve guests. One seating plan. One name crossed out.
blurb:
Philippa has planned the perfect anniversary dinner, down to the last place card. When her husband adds a name to the list in red ink, she crosses it out.
By the end of the evening, one guest is dead, and the only person who knew the seating plan is the hostess. A sharp, stylish domestic thriller.
Every guest has a reason. Every reason has a seat.
bio: Philippa Strand ran a catering business in London for twenty years. She has seen everything at dinner parties. This is her first thriller. She lives in Surrey.

title: Nobody Saw
author: Jonah Petrakis
hook: Four hundred people at the crossing. Not one witness.
blurb:
In the rush-hour rain, a woman in a red raincoat is pushed beneath a bus. Four hundred commuters were on the crossing. Every one of them was looking at their phone.
Detective Jonah Petrakis has to find the one person who looked up, before the killer finds them first.
Fast, smart and tense as a crowded train, a thriller about the city's blind spots.
bio: Jonah Petrakis is a former crime reporter who covered the city beat for a decade. He lives in London and walks everywhere. This is his first novel.

title: Vacancy at the Starlite
author: Dale Brennecke
hook: The sign said NO VACANCY. They let her in anyway.
blurb:
When her car breaks down in the desert, Dale finds a motel with a pink neon sign and one room left. The owner is friendly. The other guests are quiet.
By midnight, Dale realises nobody who checks into the Starlite ever checks out. A tense, neon-lit thriller.
Check in. Lock the door. Don't open it for anyone.
Room 9 is ready. It always is.
bio: Dale Brennecke has driven Route 66 four times and stayed in every motel that would have him. He lives in Arizona. This is his first novel.

title: The First Mrs. Calloway
author: Lorna Beckett
hook: Everyone remembers the wedding. Nobody remembers the bride.
blurb:
When Lorna marries widower James Calloway, she moves into a beautiful house with no photographs of his first wife. Not one.
Then Lorna finds half of a torn wedding picture in the attic, and starts asking the questions the whole town has agreed never to ask.
A chilling domestic thriller about marriage, memory and the woman everyone wants to forget.
bio: Lorna Beckett writes domestic suspense. She lives in a very old house in Kent, where she has never found anything in the attic. This is her first novel.

title: Ash Remembers
author: Talia Brennock
hook: The throne burned. The ash did not forget.
blurb:
Eleven years after the Cinder Throne fell, Wren Talmadge sweeps the ruins of the palace for a living. She sifts the ash for coins and buttons and, once, a ring.
Then the ash starts to move. It gathers in her hands and shows her faces, voices, the last night of the old queen. The ash remembers who lit the fire, and the man who did it now wears the crown.
Wren has one choice: bury what she knows, or carry it to the one army that might still listen.
bio: Talia Brennock grew up in a mining town in Wales and studied medieval history in York. She now writes full time from a cottage with a smoky chimney and an opinionated cat.

title: Small Fires at the Fox Inn
author: Hana Ellery
tagline: A cosy fantasy of soup, songs and one very bad fox.
hook: Soup, songs, a hearth that never goes out — and one very bad fox.
blurb:
Retired adventurer Margit Ash wanted a quiet life. So she bought the Fox Inn at the crossroads: six rooms, one stew pot and a hearth that has burned for four hundred years.
The problem is the fox. He lives in the chimney, wears a hat made of leaves, steals pies and claims to own the place. He might be right.
When a cold stranger arrives asking for the inn's fire, Margit and the fox will have to work together — or the crossroads will go dark for good.
bio: Hana Ellery bakes bread, keeps bees and writes cosy stories about kind people in difficult kitchens. She lives in Shropshire with her family and a sourdough starter named Mabel.

title: The Keeper of Small Doors
author: Odile Marchbanks
tagline: Every door in the house opens somewhere else.
hook: Every door in the house opens somewhere else.
blurb:
When eleven-year-old Odette inherits her great-aunt's house in Lyon, she also inherits a ring of forty small brass keys and one rule: lock every door before dark.
The broom cupboard opens onto a castle courtyard at dawn. The pantry leads to a sea cave. The door under the stairs leads nowhere at all, and something on the other side has started to knock.
A warm, strange portal fantasy about the keepers who hold the worlds apart, and what happens when one of them forgets.
bio: Odile Marchbanks grew up in a tall, draughty house in Lyon with too many doors. She now lives in Edinburgh, teaches French, and still checks the locks twice.

title: The Last Wild Hour
author: Idris Calloway
hook: When the sun goes down on the last wild land, the old things wake.
blurb:
The Empire has mapped every river and named every hill. Only the Wildlands are left, and the road builders are coming.
Ranger Kit Harrow has guarded the border for twenty years. She knows the rules: be home before dusk, never answer a voice in the trees, never follow the eagle. But this autumn the dusk lasts longer than it should, and something is following her home.
A sweeping epic about the last hour before the world changes, and the people who refuse to let it go quietly.
bio: Idris Calloway is a former park ranger and mountain guide. He has walked most of the long-distance trails in Britain and wrote this book in a tent, mostly in the rain.

title: The Moth Crown
author: Ilaria Venn
hook: In the Court of Wings, beauty is a trap — and she is the prize specimen.
blurb:
Every queen of the Moth Court is chosen in the same way: she flies to the light, and she is pinned.
Lady Ilse Corvane was meant to be the next. Instead she escaped the glass case on the night of her crowning, and now the court wants her back, alive, beautiful and silent.
To survive, Ilse must play the oldest game in the palace: make them believe she is fragile, while she learns to bite.
bio: Ilaria Venn studied natural history and worked for years in a museum's insect collection, which explains a great deal. She lives in Bologna and writes court fantasy full of poison and good manners.

title: The Phoenix Tithe
author: Amara Okonjo
hook: Every hundred years, one of us must burn.
blurb:
The phoenix keeps the kingdom alive. Its fire warms the fields and lights the long winter. But every hundred years it asks for a tithe: one person, given to the flame.
Adaeze has trained all her life to be chosen. She is ready to burn. What she is not ready for is the feather that arrives on the night of the lottery, half white and half black, with someone else's name written in ash.
A fierce, lyrical fantasy about sacrifice, power and the stories a kingdom tells to stay warm.
bio: Amara Okonjo was born in Enugu and lives in Manchester. She writes fantasy inspired by West African folklore and is a keen amateur astronomer and a bad but happy dancer.

title: The Pine King
author: Eira Voss
tagline: Every winter he takes one child into the trees.
hook: Every winter he takes one child into the trees.
blurb:
In the village of Harrowmere, the first snow brings a lottery. One name, one child, sent into the pine forest to serve the King who lives there. No one has ever come back.
This year the name drawn is Tove's little brother. So Tove goes instead.
The forest is darker and older than the stories said, and the Pine King is not what anyone expected. To bring her brother's name home, Tove will have to learn what the village has really been paying for.
bio: Eira Voss grew up in northern Sweden, where winter lasts most of the year. She writes dark fairy tales for adults and lives in a wooden house at the edge of a very real forest.

title: The Starwright’s Daughter
author: Lio Fenwick
tagline: She was born to map the sky. The sky had other plans.
hook: She was born to map the sky. The sky had other plans.
blurb:
In the floating city of Halcyr, starwrights draw the constellations that guide every ship home. Lio's mother was the greatest of them, until the night she vanished from her tower and a new star appeared in the north.
Now the stars are moving. Ships are getting lost. And the only map that still works is the one Lio's mother left hidden in her daughter's sketchbook.
A luminous romantic fantasy about grief, maps and the courage to chart your own sky.
bio: Lio Fenwick studied astronomy and illustration and spent a winter working at an observatory in the Canary Islands. She lives in Bristol and draws constellations on everything, including the walls.

title: A Vow of Thorn and Silver
author: Seren Ashcombe
tagline: She swore to kill the king. Then she married him.
hook: She swore to kill the king. Then she married him.
blurb:
Seren of the Thorn Court was raised for one task: to get close enough to the Silver King to slide a blade between his ribs. The wedding was her way in.
But the king she married is not the tyrant she was promised. He is guarded, clever, and hiding a curse that is eating his kingdom from the roots up. And every night their vow binds them tighter.
Now Seren must choose between the oath she swore to her people and the one she spoke at the altar.
bio: Seren Ashcombe writes slow-burn romance with sharp edges. She worked for years as a theatre costume maker before turning to fiction, and still sews her own dragon-scale cloaks for book events.

title: Tideblade
author: Oren Maddox
hook: The lake gave her a sword. Now it wants it back.
blurb:
When the waters of Lake Marrow drop for the first time in three hundred years, fisher's daughter Isla Venn walks out onto the cracked lakebed and finds a blade standing upright in the silt.
It is cold, it is singing, and it will not let go of her hand.
The Drowned Courts beneath the lake have waited a long time for someone to lift it. Some want Isla to rule. Most want her drowned. And the tide is coming back in.
bio: Oren Maddox is a former sailing instructor who now writes about water, swords and stubborn people. He lives on the Scottish coast and swims in the sea every month of the year.

title: The Unbroken Seal
author: Cassian Dray
tagline: Break it, and the war begins again.
hook: Break it, and the war begins again.
blurb:
For forty years the Treaty of Ash has kept the peace between the river kingdoms. It sits in a vault in the neutral city of Calder, sealed in red wax, and no one has opened it since the day it was signed.
When the archivist who guards it is found dead and the seal still whole, junior clerk Rosalind Thane is the only one who notices the letter inside has changed.
Now both crowns want her silenced, and the war is one broken seal away.
bio: Cassian Dray worked as a legal translator in Brussels for fifteen years and knows exactly how much trouble a single sentence can cause. He lives in Ghent and writes political fantasy.

title: Wyrmwake
author: Petra Lune
tagline: It slept under the city for nine hundred years.
hook: It slept under the city for nine hundred years. Tonight it opened one eye.
blurb:
The city of Varrow was built on a dragon. Everyone knows the story, and no one believes it.
Then the cellars start to warm. Wells run hot. And clockmaker's apprentice Pell Danner, mending the great bell in the old cathedral, feels the stone beneath her breathe.
The guilds want the dragon kept asleep at any cost. The priests want it woken. And Pell is the only one who can hear what it is dreaming.
bio: Petra Lune is a structural engineer by day, which gives her strong opinions about what is holding up old buildings. She lives in Prague with her partner and far too many maps.

title: The Europa Deep
author: Noor Halvorsen
tagline: Below nineteen kilometres of ice, something is glowing.
hook: Below nineteen kilometres of ice, something is glowing.
blurb:
The probe Halvorsen 2 melted through the ice of Europa for four years. At a depth of 4,210 metres it reached open water, switched on its lights and saw two of them.
Small. Pale. Drifting.
Then the probe went dark, and the mission team on Earth received one last image they have told no one about.
A gripping, eerie first-contact novel about the ocean beneath the ice and the people who will risk everything to go down and see.
bio: Noor Halvorsen is a marine biologist who has spent months at sea studying deep-ocean life. She lives in Bergen and writes science fiction about the strangest places in the solar system.

title: The Garden Algorithm
author: Lena Moreau
hook: Seed 0x3F2A. Growth: unsupervised.
blurb:
Botanist Lena Okoye designed the Garden to feed a flooded city: an AI that breeds plants faster than any farmer could.
It worked. The rooftops turned green, the markets filled, and the Garden kept growing. Now it is writing its own seeds, and the new plants do things that plants should not do.
A hopeful, unsettling solarpunk novel about cities that heal, machines that dream in green, and who gets to decide what grows.
bio: Lena Moreau trained as a plant scientist and now runs a community garden in Marseille. She writes about climate, technology and stubborn growing things. Her balcony is a small, unruly jungle.

title: Iteration Nine
author: Kofi Mensah-Lowe
tagline: Eight times it ended the same way.
hook: Eight times it ended the same way.
blurb:
Every loop starts at 6:02 a.m. on the same Thursday. Every loop ends at 11:40 p.m. with the same explosion.
Physicist Ama Owusu has lived this day eight times. She has tried warning people, running away and doing nothing. The bomb goes off anyway.
Iteration nine is different. This time someone else is remembering too, and they are trying to stop her.
A fast, clever time-loop thriller about choices, chances and the cost of getting it right.
bio: Kofi Mensah-Lowe is a physics teacher in London who has been told to stop explaining time travel at parties. This is his first novel. He lives in Hackney with his family.

title: The Last Footprint
author: Amara Kole
tagline: Sea of Tranquility, 2091. Someone walked here after the last crew left.
hook: Someone walked here after the last crew left.
blurb:
In 2091 the Moon is a museum. The Apollo sites are sealed under glass, and nobody has walked the Sea of Tranquility in thirty years.
So when site guardian Imani Cole finds a fresh bootprint in the dust beside the old flag, it should be impossible. The tread matches no suit ever made. And the prints lead away, toward the dark.
A tense lunar mystery about the last frontier we thought we had finished with, and what has been waiting there all along.
bio: Amara Kole is a science journalist who has written about space missions for fifteen years. Her first novel grew from one photograph she could never stop thinking about. She lives in Lisbon.

title: The Long Orbit
author: Tomas Reyna
tagline: Eleven years. One lap. No way down.
hook: Eleven years. One lap. No way down.
blurb:
The survey ship Calloway was meant to slingshot once around Jupiter and come home. Then the engine failed on the far side of the curve.
Now six crew are locked in a long orbit around the Sun that will not bring them back past Earth for eleven years. They have food for seven. They have each other, which is either the best thing or the worst.
A tense, humane survival story about patience, maths and what people become when the only way home is to wait.
bio: Tomas Reyna trained as an aerospace engineer in Monterrey and worked on satellite launches before writing fiction. He lives in Houston and still calculates orbits for fun.

title: Low Signal
author: Juno Hart
tagline: The last town with no coverage. The last place to hide.
hook: The last town with no coverage. The last place to hide.
blurb:
In 2041 every phone, car and doorbell reports to the Grid. Every move is logged. Except in Lowell, Nevada, a dying mining town in a valley the signal never reached.
When data analyst Mara Quist finds her own name on a list of people about to be erased, she drives until the bars drop to zero.
Lowell takes her in. But the Grid is building a tower on the ridge, and the town's silence is the only thing keeping all of them alive.
bio: Juno Hart worked in network security before she started writing near-future thrillers. She lives off-grid in New Mexico, where her phone gets one bar on a good day.

title: Nobody Answers
author: Ivo Brandt
tagline: We sent the message in 2031. This is the reply.
hook: We sent the message in 2031. This is the reply.
blurb:
For fifty years the Halden Array beamed humanity's message into the dark: our numbers, our shape, our place around a small yellow star. Nothing came back.
Project director Ivo Kesler is about to switch it off for good when the receiver lights up. The reply is the same size as our message, pixel for pixel.
And it is blank.
A haunting first-contact novel about loneliness, listening and the terrifying weight of an empty answer.
bio: Ivo Brandt worked as a radio engineer at observatories in Germany and the Netherlands. He lives in Bremen, where he still listens to the sky most nights with a homemade antenna.

title: Occultation
author: Sefa Adeyemi
tagline: Something passed in front of the sun. It has not finished passing.
hook: Something passed in front of the sun. It has not finished passing.
blurb:
At 04:12 on a Tuesday the star HD 140283 dimmed by ninety-seven per cent. Then another star did. Then the Sun.
Something vast is moving through the inner solar system, and it is so dark that no telescope can see it, only the light it hides.
Astronomer Sefa Adeyemi has nine days to work out what it is and whether it is slowing down. Because if it is, it is not passing at all. It is arriving.
bio: Sefa Adeyemi holds a doctorate in astrophysics and spent years studying variable stars from observatories in Chile and South Africa. He lives in Cape Town and writes hard science fiction.

title: The Patient Engine
author: Ursa Klein
hook: It has waited 40,000 years.
blurb:
On the frozen world of Kesh, explorers find a ring of black stone around a single pillar. It is warm to the touch. It is humming. And it has been counting.
Xenologist Ursa Lind believes it is a machine, built to wait for something. The colony council believes it is a weapon. They are both right.
A classic, big-idea science fiction novel about deep time, ancient patience and the moment a very old engine finally starts to move.
bio: Ursa Klein is a geologist who has worked in Antarctica and Svalbard. She lives in Oslo and writes the kind of science fiction she loved in old paperbacks.

title: Prove You’re Human
author: Ash Mirren
tagline: Select all squares with a soul.
hook: Select all squares with a soul.
blurb:
Since the Turing Act, every citizen must pass a daily test to prove they are human. Most people click through without thinking.
Then Nell Okafor starts failing.
She has a heartbeat, a mortgage and a cat. But the test says no, again and again, and the system that says she is not human is about to take away everything she owns.
A sharp, funny and frightening novel about the machines that judge us, and the strange, messy things that make us people.
bio: Ash Mirren is a software tester who has spent far too long clicking on traffic lights. This is their first novel. They live in Leeds with a partner and a very human dog.

title: A Sky With Two Suns
author: Farid Haddad
tagline: One sun rose. Then the other.
hook: One sun rose. Then the other.
blurb:
The colony on Tamar has always had one sun. On the morning of the harvest festival, a second one rises over the red dunes.
It is too close, too bright and growing. The colony's records say it is impossible. The oldest settlers say it has happened before, and that last time nobody survived the summer.
Surveyor Nadia Haddad has forty days to cross the desert and find out what the founders buried there.
bio: Farid Haddad grew up in Amman and studied geography before becoming a desert guide in Wadi Rum. He lives in Marseille and writes planetary adventures.

title: Wake Cycle
author: Remy Okoro
hook: Cycle 4,112. Awake: 1.
blurb:
The generation ship Aster carries four thousand sleepers to a new world. One wakes every century to check the course, then sleeps again.
This time Rhea Okafor wakes to frost on the glass, a cold ship, and a log that says she is not the first to wake this cycle. She is the eleventh. The other ten are gone.
A claustrophobic, gripping mystery in deep space about trust, time and the one person who stays awake.
bio: Remy Okoro worked night shifts as a hospital engineer for twelve years, which taught him a lot about quiet corridors. He lives in Glasgow and writes science fiction thrillers.

title: Behind the Paper
author: Constance Weir
tagline: Somebody wrote on the wall before the paper went up.
hook: Somebody wrote on the wall before the paper went up.
blurb:
Restoring a Victorian house in Bath was meant to be Nora's dream project. Then she starts stripping the wallpaper in the back bedroom.
Under the pretty tulip print, painted straight onto the plaster in letters a foot high, are three words. Under those, more words. Somebody covered every wall of the room with writing and then papered over it, and every layer is a warning.
The further Nora peels, the more the house wants her to stop.
bio: Constance Weir is a building conservator who has spent twenty years peeling back old walls. She lives in Somerset and writes gothic horror with plenty of dust.

title: Every Time You Blink
author: Rhys Calder
hook: Three photographs. One minute apart.
blurb:
When a hiker vanishes in the Pennine woods, all the search team finds is her camera. On the memory card are three photographs of the same misty path, taken a minute apart.
In the first, a figure stands far back among the trees. In the second it is closer. In the third it fills the frame.
Photographer Sam Calder thinks it is a hoax. Then he walks the path himself, and his own camera starts taking pictures on its own.
bio: Rhys Calder is a landscape photographer from the Yorkshire Dales who mostly takes pictures of fog. This is his first novel. He no longer walks alone at dusk.

title: Her Final Sitting
author: Edwina Crane
tagline: The portrait was finished. The face was not.
hook: The portrait was finished. The face was not.
blurb:
In 1665 a painter in Deventer was hired to paint a merchant's young wife. He finished the lace, the silver, the curls. Then he refused to paint her face, and left the town that night.
Three hundred years later the portrait hangs in a small museum, the face a smooth black void. Conservator Hanna de Vries has been asked to clean it.
The more she works on it, the more she understands why the painter ran.
bio: Edwina Crane worked as an art handler for museums in London and Amsterdam. She lives in Norwich and writes gothic stories about beautiful, terrible objects.

title: There Are Five of Us
author: Delia Marsh
tagline: Lily drew the family. She drew the lady too.
hook: Lily drew the family. She drew the lady too.
blurb:
The new house was meant to be a fresh start for the Marsh family: Mom, Dad, Ella and five-year-old Lily.
Then Lily brings home a drawing from school. Four stick figures by a red house, holding hands. And in the upstairs window, scribbled so hard the crayon tore the paper, a fifth.
The lady, Lily says. She lives with us now.
Nobody else can see her. But every new drawing shows her a little closer.
bio: Delia Marsh is a former nursery teacher who has seen a lot of crayon drawings, most of them harmless. She lives in Ohio with her husband and two children.

title: What the Moon Eats
author: Tilda Rook
tagline: The moon came up black, and it was hungry.
hook: The moon came up black, and it was hungry.
blurb:
On the night of the harvest moon in Gallows Farm, Kansas, the moon rises black. Not hidden. Not eclipsed. Black, and much too big.
By morning the cattle are gone. By the next night, so are the Pruitt family's dogs.
Tilda Rook, back home to look after her dying father, is the only one who remembers the old song her grandmother sang about the black moon. It ends with a list of what the moon eats. She hopes the song is wrong about the last line.
bio: Tilda Rook grew up on a farm in Kansas, where the sky is very big and very empty at night. She now lives in Chicago and writes cosmic horror.

title: The Night Monitor
author: Jess Varga
tagline: The baby sleeps through. Something else doesn’t.
hook: The baby sleeps through. Something else doesn't.
blurb:
After months of sleepless nights, Jess and Daniel finally have a baby who sleeps. They buy the best monitor money can buy: infrared camera, sound alerts, an app that logs every movement.
At 02:47 every night, the app logs a movement in the nursery.
The baby is fast asleep. The camera shows an empty crib. And in the corner of the screen, two small lights blink back at them.
A chilling story about new parents, tired minds and the things that watch in the dark.
bio: Jess Varga is a mother of two who has spent a lot of nights staring at a baby monitor. She lives in Toronto and writes psychological horror.

title: Only in the Water
author: Hollis Gray
tagline: Nobody stands on the dock. Look again.
hook: Nobody stands on the dock. Look again.
blurb:
Grief brings Clare Whitlock back to her family's lake house in Georgia: one long summer to clear it out and sell.
The lake is beautiful. Still. Perfect for reflections. And in every reflection of the old dock, a woman in a long dress is standing at the end, waiting. Turn round, and the dock is empty.
The locals say the lake keeps what it takes. Clare is starting to think it wants something back.
bio: Hollis Gray grew up beside a lake in North Carolina and still won't swim in it. She lives in Asheville and writes quiet, creeping horror.

title: Room 0
author: Vera Holm
tagline: The hotel has forty rooms. Your key opens the forty-first.
hook: The hotel has forty rooms. Your key opens the forty-first.
blurb:
Night clerk Vera Holm knows every room in the old Lindqvist Hotel. Forty doors, forty keys, forty red fobs on the board behind the desk.
On her first winter shift, a forty-first key appears on the board. The fob says 0. And at 3 a.m. a guest she never checked in calls down from that room to ask for clean towels.
The hotel has a long memory. Room 0 has been waiting for someone to answer.
bio: Vera Holm worked night shifts at hotels in Stockholm and Copenhagen for nine years. She lives in Malmö and writes horror about the places most people only pass through.

title: The Seventh Stair
author: Margo Fenn
tagline: Count the stairs. Then count them again.
hook: Count the stairs. Then count them again.
blurb:
The cellar stairs in the old Fenn house have six steps. Everyone who has lived there has counted them.
But at night, coming up in the dark, some of them count seven.
When Margo moves back into her grandmother's house after a divorce, she promises herself she will not go down at night. Then her son starts counting out loud in his sleep.
A tight, terrifying haunted-house novel about family secrets and the step you should never take.
bio: Margo Fenn lives in a very old house in Vermont with very creaky stairs. She worked as a radio producer before turning to horror fiction.

title: Smile Wider
author: Odette Vance
tagline: Everyone in Dellwood is so happy.
hook: Everyone in Dellwood is so happy.
blurb:
Dellwood, Oregon, is the happiest town in the state. It says so on the sign. The people smile at the bakery, smile at the school gate, smile at funerals.
When journalist Maya Lund moves there for a quiet year, the smiles feel like a welcome. Then she notices nobody ever stops smiling, not even asleep, and the town dentist wants to see her.
A darkly funny, deeply unsettling small-town horror about the cost of keeping up appearances.
bio: Odette Vance spent ten years writing for a lifestyle magazine about how to be happier. She lives in Portland and now writes horror instead. She rarely smiles in photographs.

title: A Table for Thirteen
author: Lucian Ashe
hook: Twelve guests were invited.
blurb:
Every October the Ashe family holds a dinner at the old house in the Cotswolds. Twelve chairs. Twelve candles. Twelve cousins who hate each other.
This year there are thirteen place settings. The extra card is in the same old ink as the rest, and it simply says You.
No one will admit to setting it. No one wants to sit there. And by the end of the night, someone will.
An elegant, wicked gothic novel about inheritance, guilt and an invitation you cannot refuse.
bio: Lucian Ashe grew up in a family that took dinner parties far too seriously. He lives in Bath and writes gothic horror with good table manners.

title: Do Not Play Tape Four
author: Cal Brennan
tagline: Found in the wall of 9 Ashby Lane, with three others.
hook: Found in the wall of 9 Ashby Lane, with three others.
blurb:
When builders knock through a wall at 9 Ashby Lane, they find four cassette tapes taped together with a note: do not play tape four.
Tapes one to three are a family recording birthdays and Christmases in 1994. Ordinary. Happy. Until the voices start talking to someone who is not in the room.
Podcaster Cal Brennan has listened to the first three. He has the fourth in his hand. Everyone who tells him not to play it seems very sure.
bio: Cal Brennan presents a true-mystery podcast and has listened to a great many strange old recordings. He lives in Dublin. Tape four is still in his drawer.

title: Death by Apple Pie
author: Winnie Hartwell
hook: The prize-winning pie had one secret ingredient too many.
blurb:
Winnie Hartwell's apple pie has won the Bramble Lane bake-off five years in a row. This year a judge takes one bite and drops dead.
The village is shocked. The police are suspicious. And Winnie knows her recipe by heart: there was nothing in that pie that should have hurt anyone.
Someone swapped the slice. To clear her name and save her bakery, Winnie must find out who wanted the judge dead and who wanted her to take the blame.
bio: Winnie Hartwell has baked for village shows for thirty years and never poisoned anyone on purpose. She lives in Kent with her husband and a very spoiled spaniel.

title: The Secret Ingredient Was Arsenic
author: Peggy Larkspur
tagline: Gran’s lemon drizzle. Gran’s little correction.
hook: Gran's lemon drizzle. Gran's little correction.
blurb:
When Peggy Larkspur inherits her gran's café, she also inherits the recipe box: forty years of cakes in Gran's looping handwriting.
The lemon drizzle card is the most stained, the most loved, and the only one with a correction. Two teaspoons of arsenic, crossed out. A pinch written above.
That could be Gran's idea of a joke. Or it could explain why three of her customers died in the 1980s. Peggy has a café to run and a family secret to solve.
bio: Peggy Larkspur runs a small café in the Peak District and keeps her grandmother's recipe cards in a biscuit tin. She has checked them all very carefully.

title: Belladonna in the Borders
author: Hester Bloom
tagline: Sow in spring. Keep well away from the vicar.
hook: Sow in spring. Keep well away from the vicar.
blurb:
Hester Bloom's garden is the pride of Little Wexley, full of lilies, foxgloves and plants with interesting Latin names.
When the vicar collapses at the summer fete after a cup of elderflower cordial, all eyes turn to the woman who knows exactly which flowers can kill.
Hester did not do it. But someone wants the village to think she did, and the only way to prove her innocence is to dig up the truth, root by poisonous root.
bio: Hester Bloom is a garden designer who knows far too much about poisonous plants. She lives in Sussex and writes cosy mysteries between planting bulbs.

title: Best Marrow in Show
author: Dorothy Kemble
tagline: First prize was worth killing for.
hook: First prize was worth killing for.
blurb:
The Wexley Show is the event of the year: jams, scones, dog agility and the fiercely fought prize for Best Marrow in Show.
This summer the reigning champion is found face down in the vegetable tent, and the red rosette is splashed with something that is not raspberry jam.
Show secretary Dorothy Kemble knows every grudge, rivalry and secret fertiliser in the parish. Before the prizes are handed out, she means to find out who wanted that marrow most.
bio: Dorothy Kemble has judged jams at country shows for twenty years and has seen grown men cry over a cucumber. She lives in Herefordshire. Her own marrows are modest.

title: The Cat in the Window Knows
author: Ottoline Price
hook: The cat sees the whole village. And the cat knows.
blurb:
Every morning Bramble, a black cat with a white whisker, sits in the window of the Larkspur Lane post office and watches the village go by.
When the postmistress is found at the bottom of her stairs, everyone calls it an accident. Her niece Ottoline is not so sure. Bramble has started behaving very strangely around certain customers.
With the help of one sharp-eyed cat, Ottoline follows the clues through gossip, parcels and one very suspicious window box.
bio: Ottoline Price lives in a stone cottage in Dorset with three cats, all of whom think they could solve a murder faster than she could. This is her first mystery.

title: The Dog Found the Body
author: Bridie Quinn
hook: Biscuit wanted a walk. He found a body.
blurb:
Biscuit is a scruffy terrier with a nose for trouble. Every morning he drags his owner, retired midwife Bridie Quinn, across the fields above the village.
This morning he digs up something that is not a rabbit.
The police want Bridie to leave it to them. Biscuit has other ideas. As the muddy paw prints lead from the field to the manor house and back, the pair uncover a village full of secrets and one very nervous gardener.
bio: Bridie Quinn worked as a midwife in County Clare for thirty years and now walks her terrier across the hills twice a day. Some of her walks have been very interesting.

title: Fair Isle, Foul Play
author: Morag Ferguson
hook: Every pattern tells a story. This one tells a murder.
blurb:
On the Shetland island of Fair Isle, knitter Morag Ferguson can read a jumper like a book: who made it, which croft, which winter.
So when a body washes up wearing a sweater with a pattern she has never seen, little knives knitted into the band and a skull hidden in the yoke, Morag knows it was made as a message.
With a storm closing the ferry and a killer among seventy islanders, Morag must unpick the pattern stitch by stitch.
bio: Morag Ferguson grew up in Lerwick and learned to knit before she could read. She now teaches knitting workshops and writes cosy mysteries with plenty of wool.

title: Murder at the Gilded Quill
author: Clementine Bright
hook: Closed until further notice.
blurb:
The Gilded Quill is the oldest bookshop in Harrowgate: green paint, gold letters, and a bell that has rung for every customer since 1911.
On Monday morning the sign says closed. The owner is dead in the rare-books room, and a first edition worth a fortune is missing.
New assistant Clementine Bright has worked there for three weeks. She knows the stock, the regulars and every creaky floorboard, and she knows the killer is someone who loves books as much as she does.
bio: Clementine Bright has worked in secondhand bookshops in Hay-on-Wye and Edinburgh. She lives in a flat above a bookshop, which she says is research. She has never been able to walk past a bargain shelf.

title: Death Comes to Little Haven
author: Muriel Ashdown
hook: Summer at the seaside. A body in the bathing hut.
blurb:
August 1928. The guests of the Bellevue Hotel in Little Haven come for the sea air, the promenade and the regatta. They do not come for murder.
But on the morning of the swimming race, a retired colonel is found dead in his striped bathing hut, the door locked from the inside.
Miss Edith Tremayne, a quiet lady on her first holiday in ten years, has seen everything from her deckchair. And she does not believe in locked doors.
bio: Muriel Ashdown grew up reading golden-age mysteries in her grandmother's seaside boarding house. She lives in Cornwall and writes classic whodunits with a modern eye.

title: Seven Across, One Dead
author: Prudence Pell
hook: The vicar never missed the Sunday crossword. Until now.
blurb:
In the village of Little Wexley, the parish newsletter crossword is a serious business, and retired schoolteacher Prudence Pell has won it eleven years running.
This week, seven across has an odd answer: MURDER. The next morning the vicar is found dead in the vestry with the newsletter in his hand.
Prudence knows a clue when she sees one. Armed with a pencil, a thesaurus and her nosy neighbour, she sets out to solve the puzzle before the killer sets the next one.
bio: Prudence Pell is a retired English teacher who has never finished a crossword in pen. She lives in a Cotswold village with a lot of opinions and an elderly Labrador.

title: The Tea Leaves Say Murder
author: Rosalind Pye
hook: Rosalind reads tea leaves for fun. This cup isn't funny.
blurb:
At the Teapot and Thimble, owner Rosalind Pye offers a free tea-leaf reading with every pot of Assam. It is mostly harmless: a journey, a tall stranger, good news by post.
Then Mrs Harrington's empty cup shows a perfect little skull. Two days later Mrs Harrington is dead.
The police say heart attack. Rosalind says the leaves never lie, and she has a shop full of regulars who all had reasons to dislike the deceased.
bio: Rosalind Pye ran a tea room in Whitby for fifteen years and has read a great many tea leaves, badly. She lives on the Yorkshire coast with two cats.

title: The Thousand-Piece Murder
author: Agatha Penrose
hook: Nine hundred and ninety-nine pieces. One of them is evidence.
blurb:
The Thursday Puzzle Club of St Mary Mead Lane meets in the church hall to finish a thousand-piece jigsaw every month. This month it is an old Flemish village, and they are one piece short.
The missing piece turns up the next day in the hand of the club treasurer, found dead in the vestry.
Retired librarian Agatha Penrose has never left a puzzle unfinished. With her fellow club members, she starts fitting together the pieces of a very local murder.
bio: Agatha Penrose is a retired librarian who has finished more than four hundred jigsaws and lost exactly one piece. She lives in Norfolk. She still looks for it under the sofa.

title: The Box Marked 1987
author: Hal Brody
hook: Case 87-114. Do not destroy.
blurb:
When a county evidence room in rural Minnesota was cleared out in 2019, one cardboard box was marked in black stencil: 1987. A note in marker said do not destroy.
Inside was everything left of the Pike Lake case: a muddy jacket, a cassette, eleven photographs and a detective's notebook nobody had read for thirty years.
Journalist Hal Brody opened the box. What followed was a four-year search that brought a forgotten case back to life.
bio: Hal Brody is a reporter and podcaster from Minneapolis who specialises in cold cases. He has visited more police storerooms than he can count. He is still waiting on two more boxes.

title: What the File Left Out
author: Marcus Hale
tagline: The Ferris Lake case and the 31 pages no one was meant to read.
hook: Thirty-one pages. Twenty-nine of them blacked out.
blurb:
In March 1987 sixteen-year-old Annie Doyle disappeared from Ferris Lake, Hale County. The sheriff's report ran to thirty-one pages. When it was finally released, almost every line was redacted.
Journalist Marcus Hale spent nine years fighting for the full file. What he found in the gaps was a story of a missing girl, a frightened town and the people who decided what the public was allowed to know.
A gripping investigation into one cold case and the power of what goes unsaid.
bio: Marcus Hale is an investigative reporter who has spent twenty years filing records requests. He lives in Kentucky and still keeps every redacted page he has ever received.

title: Item 47
author: Sam Delgado
tagline: A wedding ring, a bride who vanished and the ten-year lie that kept her lost.
hook: A wedding ring, a missing bride and the ten-year lie.
blurb:
Item 47 in the evidence log is a gold wedding band, found on the shore of Lake Merritt in 2012. It belonged to Elena Ruiz, who vanished three weeks after her wedding.
Her husband said she left him. Her family never believed it. For ten years the ring sat in a box in a police storeroom.
