Reporter Sam Delgado follows one small object back through a decade of lies, missed chances and a family's refusal to give up.
bio: Sam Delgado is a crime reporter in the San Francisco Bay Area. His work on missing persons cases has helped reopen several investigations. This is his first book.

title: 1414 Larkin Street
author: Celia Norwood
hook: Light on. Door unlocked. 3:10 a.m.
blurb:
In the early hours of 11 June 1998, someone walked into a quiet house on Larkin Street, Spokane, and left forty minutes later. The family inside survived. Nobody was ever charged.
Celia Norwood grew up three doors away. Twenty years later she returned with the original police photographs, still marked in the investigator's yellow grease pencil, and began to knock on doors.
A careful, haunting investigation into one night, one street and the neighbours who saw more than they said.
bio: Celia Norwood is a former local news reporter from Washington State. She now lives in Seattle and writes about crime, memory and small communities. She still visits Spokane every summer.

title: The Left Thumb
author: Ruth Kessling
tagline: A confession, a print, and the wrong man.
hook: A confession, a print, and the wrong man.
blurb:
In 1994 a man in Dayton, Ohio, confessed to a murder he could not possibly have committed. The only physical evidence was a single print from a left thumb, and it was not his.
He spent twenty-two years in prison anyway.
Ruth Kessling, a fingerprint examiner who worked on the appeal, retraces the case: the long night of questioning, the experts who looked the other way, and the thumb that told the truth the whole time.
bio: Ruth Kessling worked as a forensic fingerprint examiner for twenty-five years before turning to writing. She lives in Columbus and campaigns for the review of old convictions.

title: She Never Left the House
author: Elena Marsh
tagline: The quiet death of Ada Lowell, and the town that looked away.
hook: The quiet death of Ada Lowell, and the town that looked away.
blurb:
For forty years Ada Lowell lived alone in a white house on the edge of Fairmont, West Virginia. Neighbours waved. Nobody visited.
In 2016 she was found dead inside. She had been there for months. The police called it natural causes. The coroner was not so sure.
Elena Marsh spent three years piecing together Ada's life, and discovered a woman who had been watched, controlled and finally forgotten by everyone who could have helped.
bio: Elena Marsh is a journalist and former social worker. She lives in Pittsburgh and writes about the people that communities forget. She volunteers with a charity that supports older people living alone.

title: Nobody Hung Up
author: June Callaway
tagline: The 2 a.m. call that never ended.
hook: The 2 a.m. call that never ended.
blurb:
At 2:04 a.m. on 9 November 1993 the emergency line in Bolton County received a call from a house on Elm Avenue. No one spoke. The line stayed open. When officers arrived, the house was empty and the phone was back on the hook.
The caller was never found. The recording survived.
June Callaway, the dispatcher who took the call, tells the story of the case that never left her, and of the night she finally learned who was on the line.
bio: June Callaway worked as an emergency dispatcher for twenty-two years. She lives in Michigan and now writes about the calls she could never forget. She trains new dispatchers in her spare time.

title: The Quiet at Number Nine
author: Iris Hallam
tagline: A death in Copenhagen, 1911, and the maid who saw everything.
hook: A death in Copenhagen, 1911, and the maid who saw everything.
blurb:
In the spring of 1911 the wife of a wealthy merchant was found dead in her quiet, sunlit apartment at Strandgade 9 in Copenhagen. The police called it a fall. The family closed the case and the doors.
One person refused to stay silent: the maid, Karen Holm, who wrote down everything she saw.
Using Karen's lost letters, Iris Hallam reconstructs a crime hidden behind good manners and closed curtains.
bio: Iris Hallam is a historian of Scandinavia who has spent years in the archives of Copenhagen. She lives in York and writes historical true crime.

title: Six Miles from Redfield
author: Owen Tarrant
tagline: A girl, a dirt road, and a county that kept quiet.
hook: A girl, a dirt road, and a county that kept quiet.
blurb:
In August 1983 fifteen-year-old Lisa Kemp set off on her bicycle from her family's farm, six miles from Redfield, South Dakota. She never arrived in town.
The sheriff called her a runaway. The county moved on. Her bicycle was found forty years later, rusted in a creek bed.
Owen Tarrant spent five years in Redfield, listening to the people who knew more than they ever told, and asking the questions nobody asked in 1983.
bio: Owen Tarrant is a journalist and former high-school teacher from the Great Plains. He lives in Sioux Falls and writes about rural crime and the families left behind.

title: The Route 9 Vanishings
author: Gil Navarro
tagline: Six drivers. Forty miles. Thirty years of silence.
hook: Six drivers. Forty miles. Thirty years of silence.
blurb:
Between 1979 and 1994, six people vanished while driving the same forty-mile stretch of Route 9 through the Adirondacks. Their cars were found. They never were.
Gil Navarro drove that road as a boy. As an adult he went back with maps, police files and the families who had waited decades for answers.
A gripping, compassionate investigation into a lonely road, the stories locals tell about it, and the truth that was hidden in plain sight.
bio: Gil Navarro is a documentary maker and writer based in upstate New York. He has made three films about unsolved cases. He still drives Route 9 at least once a year, always in daylight.

title: The Shape He Left
author: Dana Ferro
tagline: Seven nights, one street, and the outline that came back.
hook: Seven nights. One street. The outline that came back.
blurb:
Over seven nights in the winter of 1991, someone attacked women walking home along one street in Leeds. Then the attacks stopped, and the case went cold.
Twenty-six years later a chalk outline appeared on the same pavement, drawn exactly where the first victim fell.
Dana Ferro, a crime reporter who grew up nearby, follows the case from the original investigation to the modern hunt for whoever drew that outline, and why.
bio: Dana Ferro has reported on crime for national newspapers for eighteen years. She grew up in West Yorkshire and now lives in Manchester. She writes in a small office overlooking a busy street.

title: Step Forward, Number Three
author: Terrence Bale
tagline: Five men in a line-up. Four shadows.
hook: Five men in a line-up. One witness. The wrong choice.
blurb:
In 1979 a nineteen-year-old witness looked at five men in a Baltimore police line-up and pointed at number three. He was sure. The jury believed him.
Number three spent thirty-four years in prison for a crime he did not commit.
Terrence Bale tells the story of that line-up from every side: the witness who has lived with his mistake, the man who paid for it, and the system that turns honest memory into certainty.
bio: Terrence Bale is a former public defender who now writes about wrongful convictions. He lives in Baltimore and teaches law at a community college. He has represented more than two hundred clients.

title: Elephant Can’t Hide
author: Ida Brandt
tagline: He is very sure nobody can see him.
hook: He is very big. The tree is very thin. He is very sure nobody can see him.
blurb:
Elephant wants to play hide-and-seek, and he has found the perfect spot: behind a skinny birch tree.
The birds can see him. The rabbits can see him. Even the snail can see him. But Elephant keeps very still, and keeps very quiet, and waits.
A gentle, funny story about trying your best, being seen, and the friends who play along anyway.
bio: Ida Brandt draws with pencil and paints with too much water. She grew up near a forest with very few elephants and lives in Copenhagen with her two children.

title: The Lantern Train
author: Margot Oyelaran
tagline: Every window has a sleepy passenger.
hook: Every window has a sleepy passenger.
blurb:
When the moon comes up, the Lantern Train leaves the hill station. A rabbit, a bear, an owl, a fox, a cat and a deer climb aboard, each one carrying something small for the night.
Across the lake and past the pines the little train goes, its windows glowing in the dark water, until one by one every passenger is fast asleep.
A soft, rhythmic bedtime read-aloud with a lullaby at the end.
bio: Margot Oyelaran paints with gouache at her kitchen table in Bristol. She once took a night train across Europe and has been drawing trains ever since.

title: Lionel Needs a Trim
author: Tomás Irela
tagline: Just a little off the top. Please.
hook: Just a little off the top. Please.
blurb:
Lionel's mane has grown. And grown. And GROWN. It tickles his nose, it hides his eyes and it gets stuck in every door in the savannah.
So Lionel goes to see Bird, who owns a very small pair of scissors and a very big plan.
Snip by snip, a story about change, nerves and the bravest haircut of all. With a big fold-out mane.
bio: Tomás Irela cuts paper for a living, and sometimes for fun. He makes picture books in a studio in Lisbon full of paper scraps and one patient cat.

title: Somebody Bit the Moon
author: Noor Haddad
tagline: And the crumbs are on the roof.
hook: Someone bit the moon. And the crumbs are on the roof.
blurb:
One night the whole town wakes up to find a bite missing from the moon. Was it the baker? The hungry dog? The night bus driver?
Only Mouse knows the truth, and Mouse is not telling. Not yet.
A bright, giggly mystery printed in three inks, about sharing, sorry, and what the moon tastes like. Perfect for reading under the stars.
bio: Noor Haddad is a risograph printer and illustrator from Amman, now living in Glasgow. She likes inks that glow, stories that rhyme and biscuits shaped like the moon.

title: Down the Big Hill
author: Kai Morrow
hook: Hold on tight!
blurb:
The first snow day of the year means one thing: the Big Hill.
It is steep. It is very, very tall. And everyone says it is too big for Mila and her little red sled.
But Mila has a plan, a hat with a pompom and exactly one brave idea. Down she goes!
A rushing, read-it-loud story about fear, fun and finding your speed.
bio: Kai Morrow grew up in a mountain town where the winters were long and the sledging was fast. He now designs picture books in Vancouver.

title: Oh No, Octopus!
author: Wren Adebayo
hook: Eight arms. Too many letters.
blurb:
Octopus is learning to juggle. One letter is easy. Two is fine. But when the whole alphabet joins in, things get very wobbly, very fast.
O! H! N! O! Can Octopus keep everything in the air before the shark swims by?
A bouncy, carved-and-printed book about trying too much at once, and asking a friend for a hand. Or an arm.
bio: Wren Adebayo carves lino blocks and prints them by hand. She lives by the sea in Cornwall, where the rock pools are full of ideas.

title: Pancake Tower
author: Ravi Okonkwo
hook: One more. Just one more.
blurb:
Little Bear loves pancakes. So on Saturday morning, Grandpa makes one. Then two. Then a stack, then a tower, then a tower so tall it pokes the clouds.
Now Little Bear has a very big fork and a very big problem.
A warm, silly counting story about breakfast, sharing and knowing when enough is enough. Syrup is not included, sadly.
bio: Ravi Okonkwo is a designer and dad of three hungry children. He has made a great many pancakes and drawn even more of them. He lives in Lagos.

title: This Bear Is Too Big for This Book
author: Hollis Maraj
hook: There is simply no room.
blurb:
This is a book. It has a cover, some pages and a story about a bear.
Unfortunately the bear is far too big for it. His ears do not fit. His paws do not fit. He has already squashed the title.
Will the bear find a way to fit in, or will he have to make the book bigger? A funny, page-turning story that knows exactly how big it is.
bio: Hollis Maraj draws with crayons that are mostly too short to hold. They live in Toronto with a dog that is also too big for most rooms.

title: Who Lives in the Hole?
author: Sunny Achebe
hook: Follow the tracks and see.
blurb:
There is a hole at the bottom of the garden. Paw prints go in. Nothing comes out.
Is it a mole? A rabbit? A badger with a bad temper? Little Jo and her brother follow the tracks, peek inside, and whisper hello.
A cosy guessing book with a big, warm surprise at the end, and lots to spot on every page.
bio: Sunny Achebe grew up in Enugu and now lives in Leeds, where foxes visit her garden every night. She writes and draws picture books for curious small people.

title: The Garden Kept Growing
author: Freya Lindqvist
hook: She only watered it once.
blurb:
Nia plants one small seed by the back door and gives it one small drink of water.
By Monday it is a bush. By Wednesday it is a hedge. By Friday it is a jungle, with bananas, parrots and something with stripes moving between the leaves.
A lush, wild story about patience, wonder and what happens when you let things grow.
bio: Freya Lindqvist is a Swedish illustrator who makes collages from old paintings, seed packets and paper. She lives in Malmö with a very small and very tidy garden.

title: Into the Puddle
author: Esme Varga
tagline: Some puddles are deeper than they look.
hook: Some puddles are deeper than they look.
blurb:
It has rained all day, and Ada has new yellow boots. At the end of the street there is the biggest puddle she has ever seen.
When she looks in, she does not see the grey sky. She sees stars, and a whale swimming slowly through them.
A quiet, magical picture book about looking closely at ordinary days. Bring wellies.
bio: Esme Varga paints in watercolour and walks in the rain on purpose. She lives in Budapest and has never once kept her feet dry. She also teaches painting.

title: Stuck in Level 9
author: Dev Arora
tagline: No saves. No restarts. No way out.
hook: No saves. No restarts. No way out.
blurb:
Arjun has played Dungeon Dash nine hundred times. He knows every coin, every trap and every slime.
But when the console glitches during a thunderstorm, Arjun wakes up inside the game, with three hearts, one sword and a level that keeps changing the rules.
To get home he has to beat Level 9. Nobody ever has.
A fast, funny adventure for anyone who has ever said "just one more go".
bio: Dev Arora wrote video games for ten years before he started writing books. He lives in Leicester and is still stuck on one level of a game from 1993.

title: The Last Wolf of Harrow Wood
author: Rowan Ashe
tagline: She went into the wood to find it. It found her first.
hook: She went into the wood to find it. It found her first.
blurb:
Everyone in the village says there are no wolves left in Harrow Wood. Everyone except Elsie, who has seen the tracks.
When her little brother goes missing on the longest night of the year, Elsie takes her grandfather's lantern and walks into the trees.
What she finds there will change everything she believes about wild things, and about herself.
A haunting, hopeful animal adventure.
bio: Rowan Ashe grew up on the edge of a forest in Northumberland. Rowan has tracked deer, foxes and badgers, but is still waiting to meet a wolf.

title: Something Under the Ice
author: Sigrid Nakashima
hook: The lake froze. Something didn't.
blurb:
Every winter, Lake Hollin freezes solid and the whole town comes out to skate.
This winter, eleven-year-old Freya hears something knocking under the ice. Then she sees the eye: green, glowing and as big as a car.
Nobody believes her. So Freya and her best friend decide to find out what has been sleeping at the bottom of the lake.
A chilling, thrilling mystery with a big heart.
bio: Sigrid Nakashima was born in Norway and grew up in Japan. She has skated on many frozen lakes and always looks down, just in case.

title: Do Not Read This Notebook
author: Pip Calloway
hook: Seriously, Theo.
blurb:
This notebook belongs to Pip. It is PRIVATE. It contains:
– top-secret plans for the school talent show
– a list of everyone who owes Pip money
– the real story of what happened to the class hamster
If you are Theo, STOP READING NOW.
A laugh-out-loud diary story, full of doodles, about friendship, older brothers and keeping secrets badly.
bio: Pip Calloway kept a diary from age nine and still has every single one. Pip lives in Manchester and doodles in the margins of everything.

title: The House at the Bottom of the Well
author: Oda Fenwick
tagline: Someone left a light on down there.
hook: Someone left a light on down there.
blurb:
Behind Gran's farmhouse there is an old stone well that nobody uses.
One night Oda looks down and sees a tiny window, glowing, far below. The next morning there is a letter in the bucket, addressed to her.
Climbing down means leaving the world she knows. Staying up means never finding out who has been waiting for her.
A magical adventure about courage, family and the secrets that live beneath our feet.
bio: Oda Fenwick grew up on a farm in Cumbria with an old well her parents told her never to look into. She did, of course. She lives in Kendal.

title: The Kite Thief
author: Juno Okafor
tagline: Whatever the wind takes, she takes back.
hook: Whatever the wind takes, she takes back.
blurb:
In the cliff town of Gale's End, the wind steals things: hats, letters, washing and, once, a whole wedding cake.
Twelve-year-old Zuri has a kite and a plan to steal them all back.
But when her kite catches a brass key that the wind has been hiding for a hundred years, Zuri finds herself racing a storm to unlock the town's oldest secret.
A soaring, windswept adventure.
bio: Juno Okafor grew up flying kites on the beaches of Lagos. She now lives in Brighton, where it is always windy and her kites are always getting stuck.

title: Midnight in the Book City
author: Marisol Teague
tagline: When the library closes, the city wakes up.
hook: When the library closes, the city wakes up.
blurb:
Max is locked in the city library at closing time. Then the lights in the books come on.
The shelves are streets. The spines are skyscrapers. And the characters who live inside them need a reader's help, because someone has been stealing endings.
With a torch, a ladder and a very rude dictionary, Max sets out across the Book City before morning comes.
A love letter to libraries and readers everywhere.
bio: Marisol Teague worked in libraries for fifteen years and always wondered what happened after closing. She lives in Madrid and writes between the shelves. This is her third novel.

title: One Dragon Egg (Slightly Cracked)
author: Lou Brennan
hook: £2. No refunds.
blurb:
Lou buys a speckled egg at the Saturday market for two pounds. The seller says it is "probably a goose".
It is not a goose.
By Monday the egg is warm. By Tuesday it is talking. By Wednesday it has set fire to the curtains and eaten the neighbour's garden gnome.
Now Lou has to hide a baby dragon from Mum, school and a very suspicious man from the market.
A hilarious, heart-warming pet disaster story.
bio: Lou Brennan once bought a mystery box at a car boot sale. It contained a teapot. Lou lives in Dublin and is still hoping for a dragon.

title: Houston, We Have a Hamster
author: Amir Solano
tagline: One small step for a hamster.
hook: One small step for a hamster.
blurb:
Biscuit is a hamster. He was supposed to stay in the classroom over the weekend.
Instead he has stowed away on the school's science rocket, and now he is floating four hundred kilometres above the Earth with nothing but a fishbowl helmet and a sunflower seed.
Can Class 6B get him home before the batteries run out?
A funny, fact-packed space adventure with a real science twist.
bio: Amir Solano studied physics and then decided hamsters were more interesting. He lives in Seville and has visited three space museums and zero space stations.

title: The Shadow Swap
author: Toby Estrada
hook: His shadow had other plans.
blurb:
Toby has always been small, quiet and easy to miss. His shadow is not.
One night, shining a torch at his bedroom wall, Toby sees his shadow stretch, grow wings and roar. By morning the shadow has walked off on its own, and something else is following Toby around.
To get his shadow back, Toby will have to be braver than a dragon.
A spooky, funny fantasy about growing into yourself.
bio: Toby Estrada grew up in Texas making shadow puppets on his bedroom ceiling. He now writes books in Austin and sleeps with the light on. Sometimes.

title: The Vanishing at Hollow Hall
author: Ivy Thorncroft
tagline: Nobody leaves the Hall after dark. Somebody did.
hook: Nobody leaves the Hall after dark. Somebody did.
blurb:
Hollow Hall has thirty-three rooms, one butler and a rule: nobody leaves after dark.
When Ivy's cousin disappears during the winter storm, the doors are still locked from the inside. Only one window was lit that night, and Ivy saw someone in it.
Armed with a notebook and a borrowed key, Ivy starts to investigate the house, the family and the secrets in its walls.
A classic, twisty mystery for clever young detectives.
bio: Ivy Thorncroft grew up reading detective stories under the covers with a torch. She lives in an old house in Bath that has at least one secret room.

title: Nobody Hangs Up
author: Mara Quinlan
tagline: Episode 12. The caller is still on the line.
hook: Episode 12. The caller is still on the line.
blurb:
Seventeen-year-old Mara runs a true-crime podcast from her bedroom in a town where nothing happens.
Then, during a live episode, a caller describes a murder that hasn't happened yet. Down to the street. Down to the minute.
The police say it is a prank. The town says Mara wants attention. And every night at 3:07 a.m., the phone rings again.
A tense, twisty thriller about listening, lies and what a small town keeps quiet.
bio: Mara Quinlan produced radio documentaries before she started writing fiction. She lives in Galway and never answers calls from unknown numbers. This is her debut novel for teenagers.

title: The Year I Stopped Being Nice
author: Tessa Okafor-Lund
hook: She's done saying sorry.
blurb:
Tessa has been the nice girl for sixteen years. She lends her notes, hides her opinions and says "no worries" when there are, in fact, many worries.
This year she is going to stop.
No more covering for her best friend. No more smiling at the boy who copies her homework. No more sorry.
It is going to be a disaster. It might also be the best year of her life.
A sharp, funny contemporary novel about finding your voice.
bio: Tessa Okafor-Lund was voted "most polite" at school and has been trying to live it down ever since. She writes in Oslo and London. This is her first novel.

title: A Crown of Seven Knives
author: Elena Vargos
hook: Seven heirs. One crown. No mercy.
blurb:
When the old king dies, his crown is forged from the blades of his seven heirs. Only one of them will live to wear it.
Seventeen-year-old Elena was never meant to be an heir. She was the knife-maker's daughter, until her father's last blade chose her.
Now she must survive a court that wants her dead, a prince she cannot trust and a crown that is already hungry.
A dark, gripping fantasy of blood, loyalty and power.
bio: Elena Vargos studied medieval history and fenced competitively for six years. She lives in Barcelona and owns more swords than is strictly necessary. This is her first fantasy novel.

title: Our Song, on Repeat
author: Nina Delacroix
tagline: One song. Two earbuds. Too far apart.
hook: One song. Two earbuds. Too far apart.
blurb:
Nina and Sam met on the night bus, sharing one pair of earbuds and one song, on repeat, all the way across the city.
They never swapped names.
Now Nina is moving to another country in thirty days, and the only clue she has is a song with eleven plays and a playlist titled "for the girl on the 43".
A swoony, bittersweet romance about music, timing and finding the person who hears what you hear.
bio: Nina Delacroix writes love stories and makes far too many playlists. She lives in Montreal and still takes the night bus for inspiration. This is her second novel for young adults.

title: Corrupted File
author: Lia Moreno-Vance
tagline: One version of her is missing.
hook: One version of her is missing.
blurb:
In 2041 everyone has a backup. Your memories are saved every night, safe in the cloud, ready to restore.
When Mira wakes up after an accident, her family says she is fine. But her file is corrupted, and three months of her life are gone.
The deeper she digs into the missing data, the clearer it gets: someone deleted those months on purpose. And they want to delete her next.
A sleek, unsettling sci-fi thriller.
bio: Lia Moreno-Vance works in data security and writes fiction about the things that keep her awake. She lives in San Francisco with too many hard drives.

title: Don’t Go in the Water
author: Harper Lyne
tagline: The lake gives everything back. Eventually.
hook: The lake gives everything back. Eventually.
blurb:
Every summer, the kids of Lyne Lake swim out to the old dock. Every summer, someone dares the others to go in after dark.
This summer, Harper's twin brother went in and didn't come out.
A year later, things are washing up on the shore: his watch, his phone, his shoes. And Harper is starting to hear him calling from the water.
A haunting horror story about grief, guilt and the things that wait beneath the surface.
bio: Harper Lyne grew up spending summers on a lake in Minnesota and has never swum in the dark. She lives in Duluth and writes with the curtains closed.

title: The Society of Burnt Letters
author: Caspian Wolde
hook: To be burned after reading.
blurb:
At Ashcombe Academy the oldest society has one rule: every letter must be burned after it is read.
When scholarship student Eli finds a half-burned letter in the chapel grate, with his own name on it, he is pulled into a world of secret oaths, old money and a death the school has spent fifty years hiding.
Some secrets don't burn. They wait.
A dark academia mystery for readers who love candlelit libraries and dangerous friendships.
bio: Caspian Wolde studied classics and spent three years at a very old university with a very strange library. He lives in Edinburgh and keeps all his letters.

title: Reversed
author: Seline March
tagline: Her luck just turned. So did the card.
hook: Her luck just turned. So did the card.
blurb:
Seline has read tarot for her friends since she was twelve. It's just for fun. It's never wrong.
Then she draws the Black Cat, reversed, and her luck changes overnight. Mirrors crack. Phones die. People she loves get hurt.
To break the curse, Seline must find out who put that card in her deck, and what they want from her.
A witchy, spooky story about fate, friendship and making your own luck.
bio: Seline March has owned the same tarot deck since she was fourteen. She lives in New Orleans with a black cat who refuses to be a metaphor.

title: The Tiger in the Wallpaper
author: Ada Merriweather
tagline: Every night it moves a little closer.
hook: Every night it moves a little closer.
blurb:
When Ada's family moves into her late grandmother's house, she gets the room with the strange old wallpaper: jungle leaves, black and gold, and a tiger hidden among them.
On the first night the tiger is in the corner. On the second night it is by the window. On the third night it is beside her bed.
As the tiger creeps closer, Ada uncovers the story her grandmother never told.
A dreamlike novel about family, grief and the stories that walls keep.
bio: Ada Merriweather restores old houses and once found a love letter behind a wall. She lives in Savannah, Georgia, in a house with very busy wallpaper.

title: Where the Wolves Sleep
author: Audra Kellan
tagline: The forest remembers who belongs to it.
hook: The forest remembers who belongs to it.
blurb:
Audra has always dreamed of wolves. Running with them. Sleeping beside them. Waking with pine needles in her hair.
When she turns seventeen, the dreams stop being dreams.
Now the old forest behind her town is calling her home, and the pack inside it wants to know whose side she is on: the village that fears them, or the wild that made her.
A lush, atmospheric fantasy about belonging and becoming.
bio: Audra Kellan grew up in the forests of British Columbia and has heard wolves howl exactly twice. She lives on Vancouver Island and writes before sunrise.

title: Rules for Breaking In
author: Bo Hargreaves
hook: Rule one: never get caught.
blurb:
Bo Hargreaves has a list of rules for breaking into places. She learned them from her mother, the best art thief in Europe.
Now her mother is in prison for a theft she didn't commit, and the only way to prove it is to break into the most secure museum in London and steal the painting back.
Bo has a crew of four, a blueprint and one week. And every rule is about to be broken.
A slick, fast-paced heist with heart.
bio: Bo Hargreaves worked as a museum guard for two summers and spent most of it planning imaginary heists. She lives in London and has never stolen anything. Officially.

title: Every Blue Thing
author: Ines Halvorsen
hook: Poems for the colour that holds everything.
bio: Ines Halvorsen is a Norwegian poet and printmaker. Her poems have appeared in journals in Oslo, London and New York. She lives on an island with a ferry, a garden and a great deal of blue.
excerpt:
I collected every blue thing:
the vein at your wrist, the gas flame,
the hour before the birds.
I kept them in a jar by the window
and called it the sea.

title: Half of Me Is Elsewhere
author: Yara Bensouda
hook: Poems from the space between two homes.
bio: Yara Bensouda was born in Tangier and grew up in Marseille. She teaches French and writes poems on the train between two cities. This is her first collection in English.
excerpt:
Half of me is still standing
on the harbour wall in Tangier,
waving at a ferry
that left twenty years ago.
The other half learned the bus times here.

title: The Low Hum of Everything
author: Oren Fairweather
hook: Poems for the noise under everything.
bio: Oren Fairweather is a sound engineer and poet. He records the noise of cities at night and writes poems from what he hears. He lives in Rotterdam with two cats and one old radio.
excerpt:
There is a low hum of everything —
the fridge, the street, your breathing
in the next room —
and on the good nights
I call it peace.

title: What the Snow Kept
author: Miko Satou-Reyes
hook: Winter poems about what stays.
bio: Miko Satou-Reyes grew up between Sapporo and Manila. She writes short poems in Japanese and English and translates both ways. She lives in Montreal, where the winters are long enough to write a book.
excerpt:
The snow kept the shape of your boots
all the way to the gate,
and then it kept snowing,
and then it kept
nothing at all.

title: Drafts for My Mother
author: Ruth Abiola
hook: Poems written, crossed out, and written again.
bio: Ruth Abiola is a Nigerian-British poet and editor. Her work has been shortlisted for several pamphlet prizes. She lives in Birmingham and keeps every draft she has ever written.
excerpt:
I have written you this letter
forty times.
Each time I cross out a little more
until all that is left is
the word Mum, and a full stop.

title: Gravity, Lately
author: Theo Annika Bell
hook: Poems about falling, and the things that catch us.
bio: Theo Annika Bell is a poet and climbing instructor from Cape Town. They write about falling, holding on and the space in between. This is their first full-length collection.
excerpt:
Lately gravity
has been taking things personally:
the cup, the shelf, my resolve.
Only you keep floating up,
light as the first warm day.

title: Orchard Theory
author: Celeste Amari
hook: Poems about growing, picking and letting fall.
bio: Celeste Amari grew up on an apple farm in Normandy and now teaches literature in Lyon. Her poems have appeared in magazines in France, Ireland and the United States.
excerpt:
My theory of orchards:
you plant for someone you will not meet.
You water what you will not eat.
You leave the ladder
for the next pair of hands.

title: Moon Hours
author: Jude Okonjo
hook: Night poems for the hours nobody sees.
bio: Jude Okonjo is a night nurse and poet from Lagos, now living in Manchester. He writes in the quiet hours between shifts. Moon Hours is his debut collection.
excerpt:
In the moon hours
the kettle is louder,
the dog sighs like an old man,
and every worry I own
comes and sits on the end of the bed.

title: honey, slowly
author: Amara Lindqvist-Oyo
hook: Poems about sweetness, and taking your time.
bio: Amara Lindqvist-Oyo keeps bees on a rooftop in Stockholm and writes poems about patience. She has published two pamphlets. This is her first full collection.
excerpt:
honey, slowly,
the way the bee does it —
one flower, then another,
the whole summer
folded into a spoon.

title: Rain Index
author: Felix Adeyemi-Strand
hook: A concrete collection about weather and waiting.
bio: Felix Adeyemi-Strand is a typographer and concrete poet. His word pictures have been shown in galleries in Bergen and Berlin. He lives in Bergen, the rainiest city in Europe.
excerpt:
rain on the roof of the bus shelter,
rain on the back of my neck,
rain in the gap between
what I meant
and what I said.

title: What My Grandmother Grew
author: Agata Wren
hook: Poems pressed between the pages of a family.
bio: Agata Wren is a Polish-Welsh poet and gardener. She grows her grandmother's herbs on an allotment in Cardiff and presses the flowers between the pages of her notebooks.
excerpt:
What my grandmother grew:
mint for the tea, dill for the fish,
marigolds against the beetles,
and me,
in the shade of her apron.

title: Every Stamp in My Passport
author: Samira Qureshi
hook: Two countries. One suitcase. Every stamp tells it.
blurb:
Samira Qureshi was nine when her family left Lahore with two suitcases and a tin of her grandmother's spices. She was thirty-one when she left London to go back.
Told through the stamps in her four passports, this is a funny, tender memoir about borders, belonging and the strange double life of the child who translates for her parents.
A story for anyone who has ever had to answer the question: but where are you really from?
bio: Samira Qureshi is a journalist who has lived in Lahore, London and Toronto. This is her first book. She still keeps her grandmother's spice tin by the stove.

title: What She Read to Me
author: Eleanor Voss-Adair
hook: Every night, one more chapter. Until the last one.
blurb:
For twenty years Eleanor's mother read to her every night, first fairy tales, then novels, then, in the hospital, the newspaper.
When her mother loses her sight, Eleanor takes the book and starts reading back.
Moving between the stories they shared and the year they ran out of time, this is a luminous memoir about reading aloud, growing up and the voices that stay with us.
bio: Eleanor Voss-Adair is a librarian and storyteller. She lives in Dorset, where she runs a read-aloud club for adults who miss being read to. This is her first book.

title: Day One, Again
author: Daniel Mbeki-Ross
tagline: A memoir of getting sober, and of getting sober again.
hook: Sobriety isn't a line. It's a tally.
blurb:
Daniel Mbeki-Ross got sober for the first time at twenty-six. He counted every day, made it to day 412, and started again at one.
This is the honest, funny and unflinching story of what came after: the second first day, the friends who stayed, the ones who didn't, and the slow work of building a life you don't want to escape from.
A memoir for anyone who has ever had to start again.
bio: Daniel Mbeki-Ross is a youth worker and recovery coach in Cape Town. He has been sober, this time, for nine years. He still keeps count.

title: Lunch, Packed by My Father
author: Anand Krishnamurthy
hook: Every lunch was a letter.
blurb:
Every school day for twelve years, Anand's father packed him a three-tier steel tiffin: rice, dal, and something new on top.
He never said I love you. He said it in lemon rice and potato curry.
In this warm, funny food memoir, Anand returns to his father's kitchen to cook his way through those lunches, and to understand the quiet man who made them.
With family recipes in every chapter.
bio: Anand Krishnamurthy is a chef and food writer from Chennai, now living in Leicester. He packs his own children's lunches every morning, badly. This is his first book.

title: Mending
author: Iris Kallas-Owusu
tagline: On a family that tore, and the years it took to sew.
hook: On a family that tore, and the years it took to sew.
blurb:
When Iris was fourteen, her family split down the middle: one parent, one country, one sister on each side.
Thirty years later, she sits down with a needle, a box of old letters and her sister's phone number.
Moving between Tallinn and Accra, this is a brave, beautiful memoir about the things we break, the things we keep and the patient work of mending.
bio: Iris Kallas-Owusu is a textile artist and writer. Her quilts have been shown in Estonia and Ghana. She lives in Tallinn with her husband and a sewing machine.

title: The House on Alder Street
author: Margaret Oyelowo
hook: Seven people. Four bedrooms. One house that held them all.
blurb:
Number 14 Alder Street had a leaking roof, a crooked porch and a door that was never locked.
For Margaret Oyelowo's family of seven, it was everything.
Through one house and twenty-one summers, she tells the story of a Nigerian family making a home in 1980s Chicago: the parties, the fights, the funerals and the night the whole street came to help.
A warm, funny and heartbreaking memoir of home.
bio: Margaret Oyelowo is a teacher and writer. She grew up on Alder Street and now lives three streets away. The house is still there. The porch is still crooked.

title: The B-Side Years
author: Rafi Delgado
tagline: A memoir of growing up loud.
hook: A memoir of growing up loud.
blurb:
Rafi Delgado's childhood had a soundtrack: his father's salsa records, his sister's punk tapes and the mixtapes he made for every girl who never called back.
In this funny, nostalgic and surprisingly tender memoir, each chapter is a song from the B-side of a tape, the track nobody skips to, but the one that tells the real story.
A love letter to music, family and the years you play on repeat.
bio: Rafi Delgado is a music journalist and DJ from Miami. He owns four hundred cassette tapes and one machine that still plays them. This is his first memoir.

title: Everything Small
author: Hannah Liesel
tagline: A memoir of a year we did not get to keep.
hook: A memoir of a year we did not get to keep.
blurb:
Hannah and her husband bought the shoes before anything else. Tiny, pink, impossibly soft.
Their daughter lived for eleven days.
Written with honesty and great gentleness, this is a memoir about the small things that hold a whole life: a hospital bracelet, a lock of hair, a pair of shoes that were never worn. And about how two people learned to carry them, together.
bio: Hannah Liesel is a midwife and writer living in Freiburg. She works with families through loss and wrote this book for the parents who come after her.

title: I Was Never Quiet
author: Josie Anaya-Brennan
hook: They told her to be quiet. She got louder.
blurb:
Josie Anaya-Brennan was sent out of class for talking more times than anyone in the school's history. She grew up to be a union organiser, a protest singer and the woman who shut down a city council meeting with a megaphone.
Funny, furious and full of heart, this is a memoir about finding your voice, using it, and not apologising for the noise.
bio: Josie Anaya-Brennan is a community organiser and singer from Albuquerque. She has been asked to lower her voice in eleven countries. This is her first book, written mostly out loud.

title: Coordinates
author: Nadia El-Amin
tagline: A memoir of the places that made me.
hook: A memoir of the places that made me.
blurb:
Nadia El-Amin has lived at nine addresses on three continents. She remembers each one by its coordinates.
In this lyrical memoir, she maps her life place by place: the courtyard in Casablanca, the cold flat in Lyon, the desert road where her father taught her to drive.
A beautiful, searching book about identity, travel and the way places press themselves into us like fingerprints.
bio: Nadia El-Amin is a cartographer and essayist. Born in Casablanca, she has lived in France, Canada and Morocco again. She draws maps of places she has loved.

title: Braid
author: Lucia Ferreira-Hall
hook: My grandmother, my mother, me.
blurb:
Every Sunday, Lucia's grandmother braided her hair. Then her mother did. Now Lucia braids her own daughter's.
Woven from three lives across Lisbon, Boston and back, this is a memoir about the women who made her: their bread, their silences, their stubbornness and their songs.
A tender, beautifully written book about inheritance, and the strength you only find when three strands hold together.
bio: Lucia Ferreira-Hall is a Portuguese-American writer and teacher. She lives in Providence, Rhode Island, and bakes her grandmother's bread every Sunday. Braid is her first memoir.

title: The Body Keeps a Garden
author: Wren Halloway
hook: Poems on healing, soil and starting again.
bio: Wren Halloway is a poet and garden designer from Devon. She began writing during a long recovery from illness. Her poems have been read on radio and printed on seed packets.
excerpt:
the body keeps a garden
even in winter —
bulbs asleep under the scar,
waiting for the day
you let the light back in.

title: Daughter of the Long Quiet
author: Amina Sowe-Larkin
hook: Poems on silence, mothers and finally speaking.
bio: Amina Sowe-Larkin is a Gambian-Irish poet and performer. Her spoken-word shows have toured festivals across Europe. She lives in Dublin and has stopped apologising for being loud.
excerpt:
I am the daughter of the long quiet,
of a woman who swallowed her songs
to keep the house standing.
I am opening my mouth
for both of us.

title: Three Ways to Leave a Room
author: Kasimir Dale
hook: Poems on endings, exits and doors left open.
bio: Kasimir Dale is a Danish architect who writes poems about rooms, doors and leaving them. He lives in Aarhus. His poems have been translated into six languages.
excerpt:
Three ways to leave a room:
slam the door,
close it softly,
or stay, and let the room
leave you instead.

title: What the Moth Knows
author: Rosalind Achterberg
hook: Night poems on longing and light.
bio: Rosalind Achterberg is a Dutch-Australian poet and moth recorder. She spends summer nights counting moths for a nature survey and writing in the light of the trap.
excerpt:
what the moth knows
and will not tell you:
that wanting is a kind of flight,
that the burn
is not the point.

title: You Are Made of the Same Light
author: Noor Al-Sayed
hook: Poems on stars, grief and belonging.
bio: Noor Al-Sayed is an astronomer and poet from Amman. She studies the light of distant stars by day and writes about it by night. This is her first collection.
excerpt:
you are made of the same light
as the things you have lost.
look up on a clear night —
they are still
on their way to you.

title: The Colour of Leaving
author: Léa Marchetti
hook: Poems on moving away and carrying home.
bio: Léa Marchetti is a painter and poet born in Corsica, now living in Glasgow. She writes about colour, migration and the families we leave and carry with us.
excerpt:
the colour of leaving
is the orange of the last streetlight,
the red of the taxi brakes,
the deep wine of the window
where my mother stands.

title: Small Rooms of Light
author: Tavi Oyelaran-Brooks
hook: Poems for the small joys that hold us up.
bio: Tavi Oyelaran-Brooks is a poet and primary school teacher in Bristol. They write short, joyful poems for people who need one. Their poems have gone round the world online.
excerpt:
I live in small rooms of light:
the five minutes of sun on the stairs,
your laugh through the wall,
a poppy on the roundabout
that nobody planted.

title: Salt in the Hymn
author: Elias Mbeki-Thorne
hook: Poems of the sea, faith and the fishing coast.
bio: Elias Mbeki-Thorne grew up in a fishing family on the Northumberland coast. He sang in the chapel choir for twenty years. Salt in the Hymn is his first collection.
excerpt:
My father sang the hymns
with salt still in his beard.
God was the tide to him:
always leaving,
always coming back.

title: Plum Blossom, Late Snow
author: Mei Hasegawa
hook: Short poems in the spirit of the ink masters.
bio: Mei Hasegawa writes haiku and short poems in Japanese and English. She studied ink painting in Kyoto and now lives in Vancouver, where she keeps a plum tree on her balcony.
excerpt:
plum blossom, late snow —
which one is falling
and which one is staying?
the old tree
does not say.

title: Hush, Little Hedgehog
author: Poppy Adeyemi
tagline: Winter is coming. Time for the longest sleep.
hook: Winter is coming. Time for the longest sleep.
blurb:
The leaves are falling and the nights are cold. Little Hedgehog is ready for the longest sleep of the year.
But first she must say goodnight to the moon, to the owl, to the last red apple and to every leaf that drifts down to keep her warm.
A soothing autumn bedtime book made with real printed leaves. Goodnight, little one.
bio: Poppy Adeyemi prints with leaves she collects on her morning walks. She lives in a cottage in Shropshire and leaves a dish of water out for the hedgehogs.

title: The Paper Fox Society
author: Hugo Asante-Reed
tagline: Fold once for luck. Fold twice for trouble.
hook: Fold once for luck. Fold twice for trouble.
blurb:
Kofi finds an origami fox on his doorstep with a message folded inside: You have been chosen.
The Paper Fox Society is a secret club of kids who can fold paper into things that come alive. Cranes that fly. Boats that sail. Foxes that keep watch.
But someone is using the old folds for something darker, and only Kofi's fox knows who.
A crisp, clever adventure full of paper magic.
bio: Hugo Asante-Reed has folded over ten thousand paper cranes and lost most of them under the sofa. He lives in London and teaches origami at his local library.

title: Deuce, Probably
author: Zoe Farah-Klein
tagline: Love means nothing. In tennis, anyway.
hook: Love means nothing. In tennis, anyway.
blurb:
Zoe is the best junior tennis player in the county, and she has one rule: no distractions before the national finals.
Then her new doubles partner turns out to be Kai, her ex-best friend, current rival and the most annoying boy she has ever met.
They have six weeks to learn to play together. Zoe is sure she can survive that without falling for him. Probably.
A funny, sun-soaked sports romance.
bio: Zoe Farah-Klein played competitive tennis until a wrist injury turned her to writing. She lives in Melbourne and still talks to herself during matches. This is her first novel.

title: Bed Twelve, by the Window
author: Cora Lindwall
tagline: A memoir of the year I learned to wait.
hook: A memoir of the year I learned to wait.
blurb:
At thirty-four, Cora Lindwall spent eleven months in hospital, in bed twelve, by the window.
She learned the nurses' footsteps, the moods of the car park, and the exact minute the sun reached her blanket each day.
Funny, clear-eyed and full of small kindnesses, this is a memoir about illness, patience and the life you can still live from one bed by one window.
bio: Cora Lindwall is a former architect who now writes about health and recovery. She lives in Gothenburg and always asks for the window seat. This is her first book.

title: Begin Badly
author: Owen Achterberg
tagline: Every good thing you love started as a bad first try
hook: Everything you admire started as a bad first try.
blurb:
Perfectionism looks like high standards. Mostly, it looks like never starting.
Owen Achterberg, a type designer, collects the terrible first drafts of good things: early sketches, rough recordings, wobbly first pages. In Begin Badly he shows why ugly beginnings are not a problem to avoid but the only way in. A short, funny and freeing book for anyone with a project they keep not starting.
bio: Owen Achterberg is a Dutch type designer and teacher. His first typeface, he admits, was unreadable. He lives in Rotterdam with his family and a drawer of very bad sketches.
bullets: Why your first version is supposed to be bad
The ten-minute ugly draft method
How to finish without being perfect

title: Charge What You're Worth
author: Nadia Brennan
hook: Your price is a message. Make sure it says the right thing.
blurb:
Freelancers, makers and small business owners undercharge for the same reasons: fear, habit and not knowing what else to say.
Nadia Brennan, a pricing consultant, shows exactly how to set a fair price, raise it without losing good clients and answer the question "can you do it cheaper?" calmly. Full of real numbers, scripts and simple worksheets, this is the book she wishes she had in her first year of business.
bio: Nadia Brennan has advised more than three hundred small businesses on pricing. She started out as a freelance illustrator who charged far too little. She lives in Dublin.
bullets: A step-by-step method to set your price
Scripts for raising prices with existing clients
When to say no to a discount, and how

title: Enough Is a Number
author: Leo Sato-Hart
tagline: A money book for people who never feel they have it
hook: If you never decide what enough is, you will never have it.
blurb:
Some people earn more every year and still feel poor. Leo Sato-Hart was one of them.
A former financial adviser, he noticed that his calmest clients were not the richest. They were the ones who had written down a number: what enough looked like for them. This clear, friendly book helps you find your own number, build a plan around it, and finally stop running on a treadmill that never ends.
bio: Leo Sato-Hart worked as a financial adviser in Vancouver for fifteen years. He now writes and teaches about money and contentment, and spends as much time as possible on his bike.
bullets: How to work out your own enough number
A simple money plan that fits on one page
Why more income rarely fixes money stress

title: Gold in the Cracks
author: Dr. Amara Lowe
tagline: On mending, and coming back stronger
hook: What broke you can become the most beautiful part of you.
blurb:
In Japan, broken pottery is sometimes mended with gold. The repair is not hidden. It becomes the best part of the bowl.
Dr. Amara Lowe uses this old craft, kintsugi, as a map for recovery after loss, illness, divorce or failure. Drawing on her work with patients and her own long recovery after an accident, she offers a gentle, practical way to heal without pretending nothing happened.
bio: Dr. Amara Lowe is a psychotherapist who specialises in recovery after trauma and loss. She also teaches pottery on weekends, badly, she says, and lives on the Kent coast.
bullets: The four stages of mending
How to talk about the crack without living in it
Small daily practices for rebuilding trust in yourself

title: Mostly Fine
author: Ruth Adebayo-Clarke
tagline: Why most of what you fear never happens
hook: Most of the things you worry about never happen.
blurb:
Three in the morning is a very bad time to plan your life. The mind fills the dark with what-ifs, and every one feels certain.
Ruth Adebayo-Clarke, a clinical psychologist, kept a record of her own worries for a year and checked how many came true. The answer surprised her. In this honest, gentle book she shares that record and the simple tools that helped her, and hundreds of her clients, sleep through the night.
bio: Ruth Adebayo-Clarke is a clinical psychologist who has worked in the NHS for twenty years. She lives in Manchester and still keeps a worry diary, now mostly full of crossed-out lines.
bullets: A one-page worry log you can start tonight
Why the anxious brain lies so convincingly
Five ways to come back to the present

title: No, Full Stop.
author: Maya Oduya
tagline: How to refuse without the guilt, the over-explaining or the apology
hook: You are allowed to say one word and stop.
blurb:
Most of us never learned to say no. We say "maybe", "let me check", or yes, and then we resent it for weeks.
Maya Oduya spent ten years as a hospital scheduler, turning down surgeons, families and managers every day. In this short, warm and very practical book she shows how to refuse kindly, without the long excuse, and how to stay calm when people push back. The result is more time, more energy and, oddly, better relationships.
bio: Maya Oduya ran hospital scheduling teams in London and Lagos for a decade. She now teaches workshops on boundaries at work and lives in Bristol with her partner and a very persistent cat.
bullets: Twelve scripts for the hardest kinds of no
What to do when someone pushes back
How to stop apologising for having limits

title: One Floor Up
author: Felix Marr
tagline: How good managers become leaders, one step at a time
hook: Leadership is not a leap. It is the next step.
blurb:
Most new leaders were promoted because they were good at their old job. Then nobody tells them that the new job is completely different.
Felix Marr has coached hundreds of first-time managers. In One Floor Up he breaks the climb into clear steps: from doing the work, to helping others do it, to deciding which work matters. Each chapter ends with one thing to try on Monday morning.
bio: Felix Marr coaches managers at growing companies across Europe. Before that he spent twelve years in operations, where he made most of the mistakes in this book. He lives in Hamburg.
bullets: The three floors of leadership and how to climb them
Hard conversations, made a little easier
A first-ninety-days plan for new managers

title: One Grain at a Time
author: Tomas Reyes Vidal
tagline: The quiet maths of habits that compound
hook: Small things, done daily, become very large things.
blurb:
An old story tells of a king who offered one grain of rice on the first square of a chessboard, two on the next, then four, and so on. By the last square there was not enough rice in the world.
Tomas Reyes Vidal uses that story to explain why tiny habits beat big plans. With clear examples from sport, money and health, he shows how to pick a habit small enough to keep and patient enough to grow.
bio: Tomas Reyes Vidal is a former maths teacher turned habit coach. He writes a weekly letter on small changes and lives in Valencia, where he is still learning the guitar, ten minutes a day.
bullets: The maths of compounding, made simple
How to choose a habit you will actually keep
What to do on the day you miss

title: Only Five Minutes
author: Tessa Okonkwo
tagline: Beat procrastination by making the start too small to skip
hook: You don't need motivation. You need five minutes.
blurb:
The hardest part of any task is starting it. So make the start so small that you cannot say no.
Tessa Okonkwo, a behaviour researcher, tested the five-minute start on writers, students, runners and herself. Most people kept going long after the timer rang. This short, cheerful book explains why it works and how to use it on the tasks you have been avoiding for months.
bio: Tessa Okonkwo studies habits and motivation at a university in Leeds. She wrote most of this book in five-minute blocks, which she says proves the point.
bullets: Why starting is the hardest part
The five-minute rule for work, study and exercise
How to keep going once the timer rings

title: Run Your Own Lane
author: Ilana Moss
hook: Stop comparing. Start finishing.
blurb:
Every day your phone shows you someone further ahead: richer, fitter, faster. It is very hard to run your own race when you keep looking at everyone else's.
Ilana Moss, a former sprinter and now a performance coach, explains why comparison steals energy and how athletes learn to keep their eyes on their own lane. Her simple tools work just as well for careers, creative work and family life.
bio: Ilana Moss competed as a sprinter for Israel before becoming a performance coach. She works with athletes, founders and artists, and lives in Tel Aviv with her two children.
bullets: The science of comparison and why it drains you
How elite athletes stay focused on their own race
A weekly reset to measure only what matters

title: Small Bets
author: Daniel Oyelaran
hook: Don't bet the company. Bet a little, learn a lot.
blurb:
Big launches make headlines. Small bets make companies.
Daniel Oyelaran has started four businesses and failed at two. He learned the most from the cheap experiments: the one-page test, the weekend prototype, the ten-customer trial. Small Bets shows founders and teams how to test ideas quickly, spend little, and only go all-in when the evidence says so. Every chapter ends with a bet you can place this week.
bio: Daniel Oyelaran is a founder and investor in Lagos and London. He has built companies in logistics and education and now advises early-stage startups on testing ideas cheaply.
bullets: How to design a small bet in one afternoon
Reading early signals without fooling yourself
When to double down, and when to walk away

title: The Unplugged Hour
author: Samir Halvorsen
tagline: Take back one hour a day from your phone
hook: One hour a day without your phone can change your whole week.
blurb:
We check our phones more than a hundred times a day, and most of us wish we didn't.
Samir Halvorsen does not ask you to throw your phone away. He asks for one hour. In this practical, kind book he shows how to choose that hour, protect it from work and family pressure, and fill it with things that make you feel like yourself again.
bio: Samir Halvorsen worked in tech for fifteen years, building the apps he now helps people put down. He lives in Oslo and spends his unplugged hour in the woods.
bullets: How to pick and protect your offline hour
Settings that make your phone less sticky
What to do with the time you win back

title: The To-Don't List
author: Jonah Kim
tagline: Forty habits to quit by Monday
hook: Your to-do list is long enough. Start crossing things off the other one.
blurb:
Productivity advice usually asks you to add something: a new app, a morning routine, a better system. Jonah Kim suggests the opposite.
After burning out at a busy design studio, he began writing a to-don't list: habits he would quit, one a week. Answering email within minutes. Saying yes before thinking. Re-reading everything twice. This book collects forty of them, with the small experiments that helped him let each one go.
bio: Jonah Kim is a product designer and writer. He has led design teams in Seoul and San Francisco and now works four days a week, on purpose, from a small studio in Portland.
bullets: Forty habits worth quitting, one a week
How to tell busy work from real work
A to-don't list template to copy

title: Where the Week Went
author: Priya Santhanam
tagline: A time audit for people who are always busy
hook: You have 168 hours a week. Do you know where they go?
blurb:
"I'm so busy" is the most common thing we say, and the least examined.
Priya Santhanam asked hundreds of people to log every hour of one week. The results were surprising: less work than they thought, much more scrolling, and almost no time for what they said mattered most. This book shows you how to do your own time audit and build a week that looks like the life you want.
bio: Priya Santhanam is a time-use researcher and consultant. She has studied how teams and families spend their hours for over a decade, and she lives in Toronto.
bullets: A one-week time audit you can start today
The hidden hours most people lose
How to redesign your week, hour by hour

title: Bread for the Road
author: Matteo Rinaldi
tagline: Forty days at the table with Jesus
hook: Jesus did some of his best work at the table.
blurb:
He fed five thousand, ate with sinners, broke bread on the road to Emmaus. Meals run all through the life of Jesus.
Over forty days, Matteo Rinaldi, a pastor and baker, explores the meals of the Gospels and what they teach us about welcome, hunger and grace. Each day includes a short reading, a reflection and a simple way to share a table with someone this week.
bio: Matteo Rinaldi is a pastor in Turin who also runs a small bakery. He believes the best sermons are often preached over a shared loaf.
bullets: Forty days through the meals of the Gospels
Simple ideas for sharing your table
Includes a family-friendly bread recipe

title: Forty Days in the Wild
author: Isaac Hollis
tagline: A Lent journey through the desert
hook: The wilderness is where God does some of his best work.
blurb:
Jesus spent forty days in the desert before he began. Moses, Elijah and Hagar all met God in the wild places.
Forty Days in the Wild is a Lent journey through the wilderness stories of the Bible. Each day offers a short reading, a reflection and one small act of letting go. It is written for anyone who feels a little lost, and wonders if that might be exactly where God is.
bio: Isaac Hollis leads wilderness retreats and walking pilgrimages across the Scottish Highlands. He has walked the length of Britain twice and still gets lost regularly.
bullets: A daily reading for every day of Lent
Wilderness stories from Moses to Jesus
One small act of letting go each day

title: Four Hundred and Ninety
author: Nathan Ellwood
hook: Peter asked: seven times? Jesus said: seventy times seven.
blurb:
Forgiveness is easy to talk about and very hard to do, especially when the hurt keeps coming back.
Nathan Ellwood, a pastor who once struggled for years to forgive his own father, explores what Jesus meant by seventy times seven. With honesty and care, he shows what forgiveness is and what it is not, and how to begin, even when you are not ready.
bio: Nathan Ellwood is a pastor and counsellor in Glasgow. He has written widely on forgiveness and reconciliation, and he and his father now meet for coffee every month.
bullets: What forgiveness is, and what it is not
How to forgive when the hurt continues
Steps toward reconciliation, when it is safe

title: Held in the Hard Places
author: Leah Moreno
tagline: Devotions for when life breaks open
hook: You may not feel held. You are.
blurb:
There are seasons when faith feels thin and God feels far away. Leah Moreno has walked through several: the loss of a baby, a long illness, a quiet depression.
These sixty short devotions are written for those seasons. Each one offers a verse, a short honest reflection and a prayer for the days you cannot find your own words. Gentle, never preachy, they are like a friend sitting beside you.
bio: Leah Moreno is a writer and speaker who shares honestly about grief and faith. She lives in Texas with her husband and two daughters and grows roses she presses into her Bible.
bullets: Sixty devotions for hard seasons
Prayers for when you have no words
Space to write and remember

title: Leave the Ninety-Nine
author: Joel Kettering
tagline: The God who comes looking for you
hook: Ninety-nine sheep were safe. He went looking for one.
blurb:
The shepherd leaves the flock to find a single lost sheep. It sounds reckless. It is the heart of the gospel.
Joel Kettering explores the God who comes looking: through the lost sheep, the lost coin, the lost son, and the people Jesus searched out. Written for the doubting, the wandering and the tired, it is a reminder that being found is not something you have to earn.
bio: Joel Kettering is a pastor and writer who works with people returning to faith after time away. He lives in Ohio with his wife and three children and a very small, very lost dog.
bullets: The parables of the lost and found
Stories of people who were searched for
Reflection questions for every chapter

title: Light Through Broken Glass
author: Teresa Lindholm
hook: Grace shines brightest through the broken places.
blurb:
Stained glass is made from broken pieces. Held together by lead and lit from behind, the pieces become something beautiful.
Teresa Lindholm writes about faith after things fall apart: a lost job, a lost marriage, a long illness. With honesty and gentle humour, she shows how God works with the pieces we bring, and how light gets in exactly where we are cracked.
bio: Teresa Lindholm is a hospital chaplain and writer. She grew up in Sweden, has lived in Minnesota for twenty years, and collects old church windows in photographs.
bullets: Faith for the seasons when things fall apart
Stories of hope from a hospital chaplain
Prayers for when you have no words

title: Mercy at First Light
author: Ruth Ellery
hook: His mercies are new every morning. So is your chance to begin again.
blurb:
Before the emails and the noise, there is a quiet moment at the start of each day.
Mercy at First Light offers a short prayer for every morning of the year, each paired with a verse and a single line to carry into the day. Simple enough for a busy morning, deep enough to return to, it is a companion for anyone who wants to meet God before the day begins.
bio: Ruth Ellery has written prayers for her church community for twenty-five years. She is a retired teacher and lives in Norfolk, where she rises early to watch the light over the fields.
bullets: A short prayer for every morning of the year
A verse and a line to carry into the day
Seasonal prayers for Advent, Lent and Easter

title: Quiet the Water
author: Grace Adeyemi
hook: When your mind is a storm, the Psalms know the way to still water.
blurb:
The Psalms are full of fear, sleeplessness and racing thoughts. They are also full of a God who stays.
Grace Adeyemi, a counsellor who has lived with anxiety since childhood, walks through twenty-one Psalms for anxious days and nights. With gentle reflections, breathing prayers and honest stories, she offers not a quick fix but a steady place to rest when your thoughts will not.
bio: Grace Adeyemi is a Christian counsellor in London. She has lived with anxiety for most of her life and writes for people who are tired of being told to just trust more.
bullets: Twenty-one Psalms for anxious days and nights
Breathing prayers for panic and sleeplessness
Honest stories from a counsellor who has been there

title: Rest Is Holy
author: Caleb Strand
tagline: Keeping the Sabbath in a world that never stops
hook: God rested. Then he told us to do the same.
blurb:
We treat rest as a reward for finishing our work. The Bible treats it as a gift we are commanded to receive.
Caleb Strand, a pastor who once burned out completely, explores the Sabbath with fresh eyes. He shows how to stop for one day a week in a world that never stops, without legalism or guilt, and why that weekly pause might be the most important thing you do.
bio: Caleb Strand is a pastor in Minneapolis. After a burnout in his thirties, he began keeping a weekly Sabbath with his family. He has not answered email on a Sunday since.
bullets: What the Bible really says about Sabbath
How to begin a weekly day of rest
Ideas for families, workers and busy parents

title: Smaller Than a Seed
author: Samuel Okafor-Penn
tagline: Forty days in the parables of Jesus
hook: Jesus told big truths in very small stories.
blurb:
A mustard seed. A lost coin. A little yeast in a lot of flour. Jesus often taught with the smallest things.
Over forty days, Samuel Okafor-Penn walks through the parables of Jesus with fresh eyes, explaining their setting, their surprise, and what they ask of us today. Each day ends with a question to carry and a short prayer. A rich, clear guide for personal study or small groups.
bio: Samuel Okafor-Penn is a pastor and New Testament teacher. He has served churches in Lagos and Birmingham and loves nothing more than a good question in a small group.
bullets: Forty readings through the parables of Jesus
Background that brings each story to life
Questions for personal study or small groups

title: The Door Was Open
author: Hannah Pruitt
tagline: Ask, seek, knock: a study of prayer
hook: Ask, seek, knock. The promise is that the door opens.
blurb:
Prayer can feel like knocking on a door that never opens. Hannah Pruitt spent years feeling exactly that.
In this warm and honest study, she explores what Jesus taught about prayer, from the Lord's Prayer to the persistent widow, and what changed when she stopped treating prayer as a test she kept failing. Eight sessions, ideal for personal study or groups.
bio: Hannah Pruitt is a Bible teacher and mother of three in Nashville. She leads a weekly study for women and writes about prayer for people who find it hard.
bullets: Eight sessions on how Jesus taught us to pray
Discussion questions for groups
Simple prayer practices for every day

title: The Fourth Field
author: Miriam Ashgrove
tagline: The parable of the sower, and the good soil in you
hook: Some seed fell on good soil. What would it take for that to be you?
blurb:
In the parable of the sower, seed falls on four kinds of ground: the path, the rocks, the thorns and the good soil. Only the fourth field bears fruit.
Miriam Ashgrove, a farmer's daughter and Bible teacher, explores what makes a heart like good soil. With practical wisdom from the land and the Gospels, she offers a six-week study on growing a faith that lasts.
bio: Miriam Ashgrove grew up on a farm in Devon and has taught the Bible for thirty years. She still keeps a vegetable plot and believes most of theology can be learned in a garden.
bullets: A six-week study of the parable of the sower
What makes the soil of the heart good
Questions and practices for each week

title: The Narrow Way Home
author: Jonah Westbrook
tagline: Following Jesus when the road gets small
hook: The road gets narrow. It still leads home.
blurb:
Jesus never promised the way would be wide or easy. He promised it would lead somewhere good.
Jonah Westbrook writes for Christians who feel the road has narrowed: fewer friends who share their faith, hard choices at work, doubts that will not leave. With warmth and steady faith, he walks through the teachings of Jesus on the narrow way and shows how to keep walking when it gets hard.
bio: Jonah Westbrook is a pastor and walking guide in the Lake District. He leads pilgrimages for people in the middle of hard seasons and believes most good conversations happen on foot.
bullets: What Jesus meant by the narrow way
Staying faithful when it costs something
Encouragement for long, hard seasons

title: The Unhurried Soul
author: Abigail Rowe
hook: God is not in a hurry. Neither is the soul he made.
blurb:
We rush through prayer the same way we rush through everything else, and then wonder why it feels empty.
The Unhurried Soul offers thirty short daily readings, each built around a single verse and a simple practice: a slow breath, a quiet walk, an unhurried meal. Written with warmth and honesty, it is an invitation to slow down long enough to notice God already with you.
bio: Abigail Rowe is a retreat leader and writer who has guided silent retreats for twenty years. She lives in the Yorkshire Dales with her husband and a garden that will not be hurried.
bullets: Thirty short readings, one for each day
A slow-prayer practice for busy mornings
Space to write after every reading

title: A Steady Heart
author: Dr. Helena Ortiz-Brand
tagline: A cardiologist's plan to calm your blood pressure, beat by beat
hook: Your heart works every second. Here is how to help it.
blurb:
High blood pressure has no symptoms, which is why it is called the silent killer. The good news: it responds well to small, steady changes.
Dr. Helena Ortiz-Brand, a cardiologist, explains how the heart works and offers a clear plan to lower your blood pressure through food, movement, sleep and stress, with or without medication. Calm, practical and reassuring. Includes simple recipes and a home blood pressure log.
bio: Dr. Helena Ortiz-Brand is a cardiologist in Madrid and Boston. She has spent twenty years helping patients bring their blood pressure down, and she walks to work every day.
bullets: How blood pressure works, explained simply
A twelve-week plan for a steadier heart
Questions to ask at your next check-up

title: Breathe Out Longer
author: Mara Lindgren
tagline: The quiet science of the out-breath, and how it calms the body
hook: Calm is a long out-breath away.
blurb:
When we are stressed, someone always says "take a deep breath". It is the wrong advice. The calming part of a breath is the way out.
Mara Lindgren, a breathing coach and former freediver, explains what really happens in your body when you exhale slowly, and teaches simple practices for stress, sleep, focus and panic. No equipment, no apps, just a few minutes of breathing you can do anywhere.
bio: Mara Lindgren is a breathing coach and former competitive freediver from Gothenburg. She now teaches breathwork to athletes, nurses and very anxious public speakers. Her own calmest moment, she says, was sixty metres underwater.
bullets: Why the out-breath calms your nervous system
Five practices for stress, sleep and panic
Two-minute routines for busy days

title: Eggs Before Eight
author: Nora Balasubramanian
tagline: A protein-first morning plan for all-day energy
hook: What you eat first decides how the rest of the day goes.
blurb:
Sugary breakfasts lead to mid-morning crashes. A breakfast built around protein can keep you full and focused until lunch.
Nutritionist Nora Balasubramanian offers a simple morning plan with thirty quick breakfasts, from eggs to lentils to yoghurt bowls, plus the science of why protein first works. Ideal for busy parents, students and anyone tired of the eleven o'clock slump. Every recipe lists its protein and its time.
bio: Nora Balasubramanian is a registered nutritionist in Chennai and Singapore. She works with schools and busy families and makes a mean masala omelette. Her clients call her the breakfast doctor.
bullets: Why protein first keeps you full for longer
Thirty quick breakfasts, many under ten minutes
Options for vegetarians and egg-free eaters

title: Her Second Spring
author: Dr. Claire Montfort
tagline: A frank, hopeful guide to menopause and the years after it
hook: Menopause is not an ending. It is a new season.
blurb:
Hot flushes, poor sleep, brain fog, low mood: menopause can turn life upside down, and too many women are told to just put up with it.
Dr. Claire Montfort, a gynaecologist, offers a frank and hopeful guide to every stage: what is happening in your body, every treatment option, and the lifestyle changes that help. A book to read, share and take to your doctor.
bio: Dr. Claire Montfort is a gynaecologist who specialises in menopause care. She works in Lyon and London and went through an early menopause herself at forty-three.
bullets: What happens in perimenopause and menopause
Every treatment option, explained clearly
Food, sleep and movement for the years ahead

title: One Less Spoonful
author: Dr. Tobias Fenn
tagline: How small cuts in sugar change everything, without a diet
hook: You don't need to quit sugar. You need one less spoonful.
blurb:
Strict sugar-free diets rarely last. Small changes almost always do.
Dr. Tobias Fenn, a nutrition doctor, shows how cutting just a little sugar, one spoonful, one drink, one snack at a time, can steady your energy, protect your teeth and heart and change your taste in a few weeks. Practical, friendly and free of guilt, this is a book for people who love sweet things.
bio: Dr. Tobias Fenn is a GP with a special interest in nutrition. He runs community food programmes in Cardiff and still has a soft spot for his grandmother's apple cake.
bullets: Where sugar hides in everyday food
A six-week plan of small swaps
How your taste buds change, and how fast

title: Strong at Seventy
author: Dr. Simone Achterberg-Lee
tagline: Muscle, balance and bone for the decades ahead
hook: It's never too late to get stronger.
blurb:
Muscle and balance fade with age, but far less than most people think, and they come back faster than anyone expects.
Dr. Simone Achterberg-Lee, a geriatric medicine specialist, offers a clear, safe strength plan for people in their sixties, seventies and beyond. Simple exercises, real stories and practical advice to stay strong, steady on your feet and independent for many years to come.
bio: Dr. Simone Achterberg-Lee is a specialist in healthy ageing. She runs strength classes for older adults in Amsterdam, and her oldest student is ninety-three. She started lifting weights herself at fifty.
bullets: A safe strength plan for every fitness level
Simple balance exercises to prevent falls
How to stay independent for longer

title: Switch Off at Ten
author: Dr. Elena Voskuijlen
tagline: The ten-night plan for deep, real sleep
hook: The secret to better sleep starts long before you go to bed.
blurb:
Most sleep advice is a list of rules nobody follows. Dr. Elena Voskuijlen offers a ten-night plan instead.
Each night you change one thing: light, screens, caffeine, the hour before bed, the hour after waking. By the tenth night you have a routine built for your own body clock. Clear, kind and backed by twenty years of sleep research, this is a plan for real people with real lives.
bio: Dr. Elena Voskuijlen is a sleep researcher and physician in Utrecht. She runs a clinic for people with insomnia and switches off her own phone at ten, most nights.
bullets: A ten-night plan, one change per night
How light and screens reset your body clock
What to do when you wake at 3 a.m.

title: Ten Minutes of Sun
author: Dr. Linnea Augustin
tagline: Morning light, sleep, mood, and the body clock you can reset
hook: The cheapest health habit in the world is ten minutes of morning light.
blurb:
Morning light sets your body clock, lifts your mood and helps you sleep at night. Most of us get far too little of it.
Dr. Linnea Augustin, who grew up with long Swedish winters, explains how light affects sleep, energy and mood, and offers a simple plan to get enough of it, whatever the weather and wherever you live. No special lamps needed, just a door, a window and ten minutes.
bio: Dr. Linnea Augustin is a physician and researcher in Uppsala. She studies how light affects mood and sleep and takes a morning walk in every season, even in the dark Swedish winter.
bullets: How light sets your body clock
Morning routines for every season
Help for winter low mood

title: Ten Minutes on Foot
author: Kwame Addo-Hart
tagline: The smallest walk that changes your heart, mood and mind
hook: You don't need a gym. You need ten minutes and a pair of shoes.
blurb:
Walking is the most underrated medicine we have. Just ten minutes a day can lower blood pressure, lift your mood and sharpen your thinking.
Kwame Addo-Hart, a physiotherapist, explains the science of walking in clear, cheerful chapters, and offers simple routes to fit a walk into even the busiest day: before work, after lunch, with a friend, or alone with your thoughts.
bio: Kwame Addo-Hart is a physiotherapist in Accra and London. He helps people recover from injury and illness by walking, and he takes at least ten minutes every day himself.
bullets: What ten minutes of walking does to your body
Easy ways to fit walks into a busy day
Walking plans for every age and fitness level

title: The Clock on Your Plate
author: Dr. Marcus Åberg
tagline: When you eat matters as much as what
hook: When you eat matters almost as much as what you eat.
blurb:
Your body runs on a daily clock, and it handles the same meal very differently at 8 a.m. and at 10 p.m.
Dr. Marcus Åberg explains the new science of meal timing: why late dinners disturb sleep, how a longer overnight break can help your metabolism, and how to fit it all around real life, shift work and family dinners. Clear, balanced and without extreme fasting rules.
